Waar kan ik de melk vinden?.scenario: You are looking for milk in a supermarket. Ask an employee where you can find it.

answers.text: Waar kan ik de melk vinden?
answers.english: Where can I find the milk?
answers.explanation: A question word takes the first position, so the finite verb comes second, then the subject. The second verb (the infinitive) usually closes the verb bracket, after the object. Kunnen is irregular: ik kan, jij kunt or kan, wij kunnen. Melk is a de-word: de melk.

answers.english: Where do I find the milk?
answers.explanation: The direct location question uses finite vind without modal kan. Both ask an employee where the milk is in this shopping situation.

Ik wil graag twee broodjes, alstublieft..scenario: You are at a bakery counter. Politely tell the assistant that you would like two bread rolls.

answers.text: Ik wil graag twee broodjes, alstublieft.
answers.english: I would like two rolls, please.
answers.explanation: A main clause has the subject first and the finite verb second. Graag comes after the verb and softens the wish; alstublieft ends the request without changing the order. Willen: ik wil, jij wilt, u wilt. Broodjes is the plural of het broodje (the -je ending makes it a het-word).
A polite counter order can be a noun phrase rather than a full clause. The requested quantity remains two bread rolls.

Kan ik met de kaart betalen?.scenario: You are about to pay at a shop. Ask whether paying by bank card is possible.

answers.text: Kan ik met de kaart betalen?
answers.explanation: This is a yes/no question. With no question word, it begins with the finite verb (Kan), and the subject (ik) follows it. The other verb parts are not conjugated: the infinitive (betalen) normally occurs toward the end. Kan ik: ik kan. Kaart is a de-word: de kaart.

Hoeveel kost deze tas?.scenario: You are pointing to a bag with no price tag. Ask its price.

answers.english: How much does this bag cost?
answers.explanation: This is a question. The question word or phrase (Hoeveel) takes the first position, so the finite verb (kost) comes second and the subject (deze tas) follows it: question word + finite verb + subject. Kosten: het kost, ze kosten. Tas is a de-word, so deze (a het-word would take dit).

answers.english: How much does this bag cost?
answers.explanation: Wat kost ...? is a standard way to ask the price, just like Hoeveel kost ...? Tas is a de-word, so deze remains correct.

Heeft u ook een kleinere maat?.scenario: The item you tried on is too big. Politely ask the assistant whether they also have a smaller size.

answers.text: Heeft u ook een kleinere maat?
answers.english: Do you also have a smaller size?
answers.explanation: This is a yes/no question. With no question word, it begins with the finite verb (Heeft), and the subject (u) follows it. With hebben, u takes either heeft or hebt; both are standard. Other verbs can differ, so do not assume u always copies hij. Kleinere is kleiner plus -e: after een with a de-word (maat) the adjective takes -e.

answers.text: Hebt u ook een kleinere maat?
answers.english: Do you also have a smaller size?
answers.explanation: Heeft u and hebt u are both standard with polite subject u. This is not the informal heb je inversion pattern.

Ik heb geen zak nodig..scenario: A cashier offers you a shopping bag. Tell them that you do not need a bag.

answers.english: I do not need a bag.
answers.explanation: A main clause: subject, then finite verb. Nodig completes the expression nodig hebben and normally occurs toward the end. Hebben: ik heb. Geen replaces een in a negative sentence: een zak becomes geen zak.

Mag ik de bon, alstublieft?.scenario: You have paid for your shopping. Politely ask the cashier for the receipt.

answers.english: May I have the receipt, please?
answers.explanation: This is a yes/no question. With no question word, it begins with the finite verb (Mag), and the subject (ik) follows it. Mogen: ik mag, jij mag, wij mogen. Bon is a de-word.

answers.text: Mag ik de bon hebben, alstublieft?
answers.english: May I have the receipt, please?
answers.explanation: Hebben makes the understood action explicit after mag. It is an infinitive without te; the polite request stays the same.

Deze appels zijn goedkoper..scenario: You are comparing two sets of apples. Point to the less expensive ones and explain the price difference.

answers.explanation: A main clause with the subject first and the finite verb second. After zijn the adjective takes no -e. A plural subject needs zijn, not is. Goedkoper is goedkoop plus -er.

Ik zoek een cadeau voor mijn vriendin..scenario: A shop assistant asks what you are looking for. Explain that you want a present for your girlfriend.

answers.text: Ik zoek een cadeau voor mijn vriendin.
answers.english: I am looking for a gift for my girlfriend.
answers.explanation: In a normal main clause the subject (Ik) comes first and the finite verb (zoek) second (verb-second order). Zoeken: ik zoek. Mijn does not change before de- or het-words. Cadeau is a het-word.

Ik neem deze, bedankt..scenario: You are choosing between bags in a shop and point to one bag (de tas). Tell the assistant you will take this one, and thank them.

answers.english: I will take this one, thank you.
answers.explanation: In a normal main clause the subject (Ik) comes first and the finite verb (neem) second (verb-second order). Nemen: ik neem. Deze stands for a de-word or plural you are pointing at; a het-word needs dit.

Kunt u dat nog eens uitleggen?.scenario: Your teacher has explained something, but you have not understood it. Politely ask for the explanation again.

answers.text: Kunt u dat nog eens uitleggen?
answers.explanation: This is a yes/no question. With no question word, it begins with the finite verb (Kunt), and the subject (u) follows it. The other verb parts are not conjugated: the infinitive (uitleggen) normally occurs toward the end. Kunnen with u: u kunt (u kan is also used). Uitleggen is a separable verb but stays whole after a modal.

answers.text: Kan u dat nog eens uitleggen?
answers.explanation: Kunt u and kan u are both standard; kan u is particularly common in Belgium. U keeps polite address and the action remains an infinitive.

answers.text: Zou u dat nog eens kunnen uitleggen?
answers.explanation: Zou u ... kunnen + infinitive phrases the same request more tentatively/politely. Kunnen is an infinitive after zou; the action also remains an infinitive. This is a present polite request, not a report about a past ability.

Ik begrijp deze vraag niet..scenario: You are pointing to a question in an exercise. Tell your teacher that you do not understand it.

answers.english: I do not understand this question.
answers.explanation: In a normal main clause the subject (Ik) comes first and the finite verb (begrijp) second (verb-second order). Begrijpen: ik begrijp (the prefix be- means no ge- in the participle: begrepen). Vraag is a de-word, so deze.

Wat betekent dit woord?.scenario: A word in your textbook is new to you. Ask your teacher what that particular word means.

answers.explanation: This is a question. The question word or phrase (Wat) takes the first position, so the finite verb (betekent) comes second and the subject (dit woord) follows it: question word + finite verb + subject. Betekenen: het betekent. Woord is a het-word, so dit.

Mag ik even iets vragen?.scenario: Your teacher is speaking. Ask politely for permission to ask a brief question.

answers.explanation: This is a yes/no question. With no question word, it begins with the finite verb (Mag), and the subject (ik) follows it. The other verb parts are not conjugated: the infinitive (vragen) normally occurs toward the end. Mag is the first-person singular of mogen. Iets means something and vragen is the infinitive. Even softens the request and suggests taking a moment; it does not demand that the question be spoken at high speed.

Ik heb mijn huiswerk al gemaakt..scenario: Your teacher asks whether your homework is finished. Explain that you have already done it.

answers.text: Ik heb mijn huiswerk al gemaakt.
answers.english: I have already done my homework.
answers.explanation: In the perfect tense the auxiliary is the finite verb in second position and the participle normally occurs toward the end. This perfect uses hebben: ik heb mijn huiswerk gemaakt. Heb is finite and gemaakt is the participle of maken. Al means already. Mijn is possessive my and stays the same before de- and het-words. The perfect does not always use hebben: some verbs and meanings use zijn, as in ik ben vertrokken.

Wanneer moeten we dit inleveren?.scenario: You and your classmates must submit an assignment. Ask when your group has to hand it in.

answers.english: When do we have to hand this in?
answers.explanation: A question word first, then the finite verb, then the subject. The infinitive normally occurs toward the end. Moeten: wij moeten. Inleveren is separable (lever ... in), but it stays whole after a modal.

answers.english: When do we have to hand this in?
answers.explanation: Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Mijn pen ligt op tafel..scenario: Someone asks where your pen is. Explain that it is lying on the table.

answers.english: My pen is on the table.
answers.explanation: In a normal main clause the subject (Mijn pen) comes first and the finite verb (ligt) second (verb-second order). Liggen: het ligt. Op tafel has no article, which is normal in this fixed phrase (op de tafel is also possible).

answers.english: My pen is on the table.
answers.explanation: Is gives the location without describing how the pen is positioned. Ligt is more specific for a pen lying down; both convey its location here.

Morgen ga ik naar school..scenario: A friend asks about tomorrow's plans. Tell them that you are going to school tomorrow.

answers.english: Tomorrow I am going to school.
answers.explanation: When a time word is first, the finite verb must still be second, so it comes before the subject (inversion). Gaan: ik ga. Naar school has no article.

answers.english: Tomorrow I am going to school.
answers.explanation: The subject is first and ga remains second. Morgen still gives the future time of the planned school visit.

Ik ben te laat omdat mijn trein vertragi.scenario: You arrive late to class because your train is delayed. Explain both your lateness and its cause.

answers.text: Ik ben te laat omdat mijn trein vertraging heeft.
answers.english: I am late because my train is delayed.
answers.explanation: After omdat the clause is subordinate, so the finite verb usually closes the verb bracket. In the main clause the verb stays second. Zijn: ik ben. Vertraging hebben means to be delayed.

Kunnen we samen oefenen?.scenario: You would like a classmate to practise with you. Ask whether the two of you can practise together.

answers.explanation: This is a yes/no question. With no question word, it begins with the finite verb (Kunnen), and the subject (we) follows it. The other verb parts are not conjugated: the infinitive (oefenen) normally occurs toward the end. Kunnen with we: we kunnen.
Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Van welk spoor vertrekt de trein?.scenario: You are at a railway station, ready to travel. Ask which platform the train departs from.

answers.text: Van welk spoor vertrekt de trein?
answers.english: From which platform does the train depart?
answers.explanation: This is a question. The question word or phrase (Van welk spoor) takes the first position, so the finite verb (vertrekt) comes second and the subject (de trein) follows it: question word + finite verb + subject. Vertrekken is irregular: ik vertrek, hij vertrekt; past vertrok/vertrokken; perfect is vertrokken. Welk modifies singular het spoor; welke modifies a singular de-word or a plural.

Moet ik hier overstappen?.scenario: You are unsure whether this is your interchange station. Ask whether you need to change trains here.

answers.english: Do I need to change trains here?
answers.explanation: This is a yes/no question. With no question word, it begins with the finite verb (Moet), and the subject (ik) follows it. The other verb parts are not conjugated: the infinitive (overstappen) normally occurs toward the end. Moeten: ik moet. Here moet is finite, so overstappen stays together as an infinitive. When overstappen itself is finite in a main clause, it splits: ik stap over. Perfect: ik ben overgestapt. Overstappen means transferring from one vehicle or connection to another, not necessarily only trains.

Gaat deze trein naar Brugge?.scenario: You are about to board a train. Check whether this particular train goes to Bruges.

answers.english: Does this train go to Bruges?
answers.explanation: This is a yes/no question. With no question word, it begins with the finite verb (Gaat), and the subject (deze trein) follows it. Gaan: de trein gaat. Trein is a de-word, so deze.

Ik wil een ticket naar Gent, alstublieft.scenario: You are at the ticket counter. Politely tell the assistant that you would like a ticket to Ghent.

answers.text: Ik wil een ticket naar Gent, alstublieft.
answers.english: I would like a ticket to Ghent, please.
answers.explanation: In a normal main clause the subject (Ik) comes first and the finite verb (wil) second (verb-second order). Willen: ik wil. Ticket is a het-word (een ticket).

Hoe laat komt de trein aan?.scenario: A friend's train has not arrived yet. Ask what time the train arrives.

answers.text: Hoe laat komt de trein aan?
answers.english: What time does the train arrive?
answers.explanation: This is a question. The question word or phrase (Hoe laat) takes the first position, so the finite verb (komt) comes second and the subject (de trein) follows it: question word + finite verb + subject. The other verb parts are not conjugated: the separable particle (aan) normally occurs toward the end while the verb itself stays second. Aankomen is separable: de trein komt ... aan.

Is deze plaats vrij?.scenario: You see a seat that appears empty. Ask another passenger whether that seat is available.

answers.explanation: This is a yes/no question. With no question word, it begins with the finite verb (Is), and the subject (deze plaats) follows it. After zijn the adjective takes no -e: vrij. Plaats is a de-word, so deze.

Mijn trein heeft tien minuten vertraging.scenario: Your train is delayed by ten minutes. Tell the person who is waiting for you about your train's delay.

answers.text: Mijn trein heeft tien minuten vertraging.
answers.english: My train is ten minutes delayed.
answers.explanation: A main clause: subject first, finite verb second. The duration comes before vertraging. Hebben: de trein heeft. Vertraging hebben means to be delayed.

answers.text: Mijn trein is tien minuten te laat.
answers.english: My train is ten minutes late.
answers.explanation: Te laat zijn gives the lateness directly. Heeft vertraging uses the noun for delay. The train and the ten-minute amount are unchanged.

Waar kan ik mijn ticket kopen?.scenario: You need to buy your train ticket. Ask someone where you can buy it.

answers.text: Waar kan ik mijn ticket kopen?
answers.english: Where can I buy my ticket?
answers.explanation: A question word first, then the finite verb, then the subject. The infinitive normally occurs toward the end. Kunnen: ik kan. Ticket is a het-word.

Ik stap bij de volgende halte uit..scenario: You are travelling by bus and your stop is next. Tell another passenger where you are getting off.

answers.text: Ik stap bij de volgende halte uit.
answers.english: I am getting off at the next stop.
answers.explanation: A main clause: subject, finite verb, then the rest. The particle uit normally occurs toward the end. Uitstappen is separable: ik stap ... uit. Volgende takes -e before the de-word halte.

Kunt u mij helpen met mijn bagage?.scenario: Your luggage is difficult to manage. Politely ask another person to help you with it.

answers.text: Kunt u mij helpen met mijn bagage?
answers.english: Can you help me with my luggage?
answers.explanation: Kunt is the finite modal and starts this polite yes/no question, followed by subject u. Mij is the person receiving help. Helpen stays an infinitive after kunt. The full prepositional phrase met mijn bagage naturally follows helpen here; closing the verb bracket does not mean being the last word of the sentence. Kunnen: u kunt or u kan; both are standard. Mij means me, while mijn means my. Helpen met iets means help with something. Kunt u mij met mijn bagage helpen? is another natural order.

answers.text: Kan u mij helpen met mijn bagage?
answers.english: Can you help me with my luggage?
answers.explanation: Kunt u and kan u are both standard; kan u is particularly common in Belgium. U keeps polite address and the action remains an infinitive.

answers.text: Kunt u me helpen met mijn bagage?
answers.english: Can you help me with my luggage?
answers.explanation: Me is the unstressed object form corresponding to full mij. The receiver or other object remains the same; the original full form can carry emphasis.

Waar zijn mijn sleutels?.scenario: You are ready to leave home, but cannot find your keys. Ask where your keys are.

answers.explanation: This is a question. The question word or phrase (Waar) takes the first position, so the finite verb (zijn) comes second and the subject (mijn sleutels) follows it: question word + finite verb + subject. Zijn agrees with the plural subject: sleutels zijn. Mijn does not change.

Ik ben aan het koken..scenario: Someone phones and asks what you are doing right now. Explain that you are cooking.

answers.explanation: In a normal main clause the subject (Ik) comes first and the finite verb (ben) second (verb-second order). The other verb parts are not conjugated: the infinitive (koken) normally occurs toward the end. Zijn: ik ben. After aan het the verb is an infinitive, not conjugated.
Dutch simple present can describe an action happening now. It does not need a separate progressive auxiliary in this context.

Heb je de deur op slot gedaan?.scenario: You are leaving the house with a friend. Ask whether they have locked the door.

answers.text: Heb je de deur op slot gedaan?
answers.explanation: This is a yes/no question. With no question word, it begins with the finite verb (Heb), and the subject (je) follows it. The other verb parts are not conjugated: the participle (gedaan) normally occurs toward the end. This perfect uses hebben: heb je ... gedaan? Doen has participle gedaan. Compare statement je hebt and question heb je: subject je follows the auxiliary, so the ordinary added -t is omitted. De deur op slot doen means lock the door. Other perfects may use zijn, depending on verb and meaning.

answers.text: Heb jij de deur op slot gedaan?
answers.explanation: Jij and je refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Ik heb de afwas al gedaan..scenario: Your housemate asks whether the dishes still need doing. Explain that you have already done them.

answers.text: Ik heb de afwas al gedaan.
answers.english: I have already washed the dishes.
answers.explanation: In the perfect tense the auxiliary is second and the participle normally occurs toward the end. Perfect: ik heb gedaan. De afwas doen means to do the dishes.

Kun je het raam openmaken?.scenario: The room needs fresh air. Ask someone to open the window.

answers.explanation: This is a yes/no question. With no question word, it begins with the finite verb (Kun), and the subject (je) follows it. The other verb parts are not conjugated: the infinitive (openmaken) normally occurs toward the end. Kunnen with je: kun je (the -t drops when subject je/jij follows the finite verb). Raam is a het-word.
Jij and je refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.
Kun je and kan je are both standard forms of kunnen with subject je. The action still follows as an infinitive.

answers.text: Zou je het raam kunnen openmaken?
answers.explanation: Zou je ... kunnen + infinitive phrases the same request more tentatively/politely. Kunnen is an infinitive after zou; the action also remains an infinitive. This is a present polite request, not a report about a past ability.

Dit is jouw kopje..scenario: You are identifying the cups on a table. Point to one and tell the person you are addressing that it belongs to them.

answers.explanation: In a normal main clause the subject (Dit) comes first and the finite verb (is) second (verb-second order). Dit is a standalone demonstrative introducing an identification: dit is jouw kopje. It is not an adjective attached to kopje. Dutch can also say Dit is jouw tas even though tas is a de-word. Before a noun directly, use dit kopje but deze tas. Jouw/je means your; jou is the object form you.
Jouw and possessive je both mean your here. Jouw is the full form and can emphasise ownership; je is unstressed. This je is not the subject.

Na het werk fiets ik naar huis..scenario: A colleague asks about your usual journey home. Explain that you cycle home after work.

answers.text: Na het werk fiets ik naar huis.
answers.explanation: Na het werk is one time constituent in first position. Fiets is the finite verb in second position, followed by subject ik. Second position means second constituent, not second word. Fietsen: ik fiets. Naar huis means home.

answers.text: Ik fiets na het werk naar huis.
answers.explanation: The subject comes first and fiets remains the second constituent. Na het werk now occurs inside the main clause.

Er staat melk in de koelkast..scenario: Someone is looking for milk. Tell them that there is milk in the fridge.

answers.text: Er staat melk in de koelkast.
answers.english: There is milk in the fridge.
answers.explanation: Er comes first, the verb second, then the real subject. Dutch uses staat for things standing or placed somewhere. Staan: singular er staat, plural er staan. Milk is understood through its container here, such as a standing carton or bottle. Compare Er staan twee pakken melk in de koelkast. Er is melk is also grammatical and simply states availability.

answers.text: Er is melk in de koelkast.
answers.english: There is milk in the fridge.
answers.explanation: Is describes availability without specifying position. Staat can picture a milk container standing in the fridge; is is not ungrammatical.

Ik ruim mijn kamer op..scenario: Someone asks what you are doing in your bedroom. Explain that you are tidying it, putting things back in place.

answers.explanation: A main clause: the verb is second and the separable particle op normally occurs toward the end. Opruimen means tidy up or put things away: ik ruim ... op; perfect ik heb opgeruimd. Schoonmaken means clean dirt away: ik maak ... schoon; perfect ik heb schoongemaakt. You can tidy a room without cleaning it, or clean its floor after putting things away.

Zullen we samen eten?.scenario: It is time for a meal. Suggest that you and the person you are addressing eat together.

answers.explanation: Zullen we plus an infinitive makes a suggestion. The question starts with the finite verb and ends with the infinitive. Zullen: wij zullen.
Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.
Laten we + infinitive makes the shared suggestion directly. Zullen we asks it as a proposal. Both fit this invitation to do the activity together.

Ik spreek een beetje Nederlands..scenario: You meet someone who speaks Dutch. Explain that you speak a little Dutch.

answers.explanation: In a normal main clause the subject (Ik) comes first and the finite verb (spreek) second (verb-second order). Spreken: ik spreek, jij/hij spreekt, wij spreken; simple past sprak/spraken; perfect heb/heeft gesproken. Een beetje means a little. The language name has no article in een beetje Nederlands spreken. An article is possible in other constructions, such as het Nederlands van vandaag (the Dutch of today).

Kun je wat langzamer spreken?.scenario: You are struggling to follow someone because they speak quickly. Ask them to speak a little more slowly.

answers.english: Can you speak a little more slowly?
answers.explanation: This is a yes/no question. With no question word, it begins with the finite verb (Kun), and the subject (je) follows it. The other verb parts are not conjugated: the infinitive (spreken) normally occurs toward the end. Kun je: the -t drops when subject je/jij follows the finite verb. Langzamer is the comparative of langzaam.

answers.english: Can you speak a little more slowly?
answers.explanation: Jij and je refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

answers.english: Can you speak a little more slowly?
answers.explanation: Kun je and kan je are both standard forms of kunnen with subject je. The action still follows as an infinitive.

answers.text: Zou je wat langzamer kunnen spreken?
answers.english: Could you speak a little more slowly?
answers.explanation: Zou je ... kunnen + infinitive phrases the same request more tentatively/politely. Kunnen is an infinitive after zou; the action also remains an infinitive. This is a present polite request, not a report about a past ability.

Hoe gaat het met je?.scenario: You greet a friend and want to know how they are doing. Ask them.

answers.explanation: This is a question. The question word or phrase (Hoe) takes the first position, so the finite verb (gaat) comes second and the subject (het) follows it: question word + finite verb + subject. Gaan: het gaat. Met je (informal) or met u (polite).

Ik woon in Roeselare..scenario: Someone asks which city you live in. Tell them that you live in Roeselare.

answers.explanation: In a normal main clause the subject (Ik) comes first and the finite verb (woon) second (verb-second order). Wonen: ik woon, jij woont, wij wonen; past woonde/woonden; perfect heb gewoond. With this city name use in Roeselare. Also in Gent and in België. This is not a claim that every geographical name always takes in.

Waar kom je vandaan?.scenario: You are getting to know someone. Ask where they are originally from.

answers.explanation: This is a question. The question word or phrase (Waar) takes the first position, so the finite verb (kom) comes second and the subject (je) follows it: question word + finite verb + subject. Komen: je komt, but the -t drops when je follows: kom je.
Jij and je refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Heb je morgen tijd?.scenario: You want to arrange something with a friend tomorrow. Ask whether they have time tomorrow.

answers.explanation: This is a yes/no question. With no question word, it begins with the finite verb (Heb), and the subject (je) follows it. Heb je: the -t of hebt drops when subject je/jij follows the finite verb.
Jij and je refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Ik kan vandaag niet komen..scenario: You were expected to come today, but cannot. Tell the other person you cannot come today.

answers.explanation: A main clause: subject then finite verb. Niet comes before the infinitive at the end. Kunnen: ik kan.

The time phrase and subject exchange main-clause positions around the finite verb. One whole constituent is first, the finite verb is second, and the subject follows it if time is first. The event and time are unchanged.

Zullen we om drie uur afspreken?.scenario: You are arranging to meet a friend. Suggest meeting at three o'clock.

answers.text: Zullen we om drie uur afspreken?
answers.english: Shall we meet at three o’clock?
answers.explanation: A suggestion starts with Zullen we, and the infinitive normally occurs toward the end. Om drie uur gives a clock time. Afspreken stays whole after zullen.

answers.text: Zullen wij om drie uur afspreken?
answers.english: Shall we meet at three o’clock?
answers.explanation: Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

answers.text: Laten we om drie uur afspreken.
answers.explanation: Laten we + infinitive makes the shared suggestion directly. Zullen we asks it as a proposal. Both fit this invitation to do the activity together.

Ik ben moe, maar ik voel me goed..scenario: A friend asks how you feel. Explain that you are tired, but otherwise feel good.

answers.text: Ik ben moe, maar ik voel me goed.
answers.english: I am tired, but I feel good.
answers.explanation: Maar joins two main clauses, so each keeps its own verb in second position. Zich voelen: ik voel me. After zijn and voelen the adjective takes no -e.

Bedankt voor je hulp..scenario: Someone has helped you. Thank them specifically for that help, using informal address.

Hij maakt zich zorgen over het verliezen.scenario: A man is anxious that he might lose his keys. Tell someone what he is worried about, rather than saying the keys are already lost.

Wat is de huidige wisselkoers?.scenario: You are at a currency exchange desk. Ask what the exchange rate is at the moment.

Ik betaal met mijn creditcard..scenario: A cashier asks how you are paying. Explain that you are using your credit card.

Het is erg mistig..scenario: You look outside and can hardly see through the fog. Describe how foggy it is.

Ik had het brood al gebakken..scenario: You are recalling a past visit. Before the visitors arrived, you had already baked the bread. Explain what was already done.

The other verb parts are not conjugated: the participle (gebakken) normally occurs toward the end. Had plus participle is the past perfect: something done before another moment in the past. Ik controleer de voorraad..scenario: A colleague asks what you are doing at work. Explain that you are checking the stock.

Rusten is goed voor je..scenario: A friend is exhausted and reluctant to rest. Explain that resting is good for them.

Wat is uw mening hierover?.scenario: You have discussed an issue with someone you address formally. Ask their opinion about that issue.

Waar ging zij heen?.scenario: A woman has left, and you do not know her destination. Ask where she went.

Ik zal een rapport opstellen..scenario: Your colleague needs a report. Say that you will prepare one.

answers.explanation: Zij and ze refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

We hebben urenlang gepraat..scenario: You and some friends have finished a conversation that lasted for hours. Tell someone about its length.

Ik houd u op de hoogte..scenario: Someone you address formally is waiting for updates. Promise to keep that person informed.

Het is half zes..scenario: Someone asks you the time. The clock shows 5:30. Tell them the time in Dutch.

Hij is een uur geleden vertrokken..scenario: Someone asks when a man left. Explain that his departure was one hour ago.

Ik ben het daarmee eens..scenario: Someone has just made a suggestion that you agree with. Tell them that you agree with it.

Dat is een geweldig idee!.scenario: A friend has made an excellent suggestion. Respond enthusiastically by calling it a great idea.

Het is het proberen waard..scenario: An idea might work, but nobody has tested it. Explain that trying it would be worthwhile.

answers.explanation: We is first and the finite present verb overwegen is second. Alle opties is its direct object. Overwegen here means consider and is inseparable. Alle goes directly before the plural noun opties in this phrase.
Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Ik heb mijn training voltooid..scenario: Someone asks about your training. Explain that you have completed it.

answers.explanation: Ik is first and the finite verb Heb is second; voltooid, the participle, closes the perfect-tense bracket at the end, after mijn training. Voltooien takes hebben in this transitive use. Voltooid ends in d; it is not voltooit, which can be a finite present form. Mijn specifies whose training.

Ik heb zijn goedkeuring nodig..scenario: A man must approve something before you can proceed. Explain that you need his approval.

answers.explanation: Heb is second. The thing needed, zijn goedkeuring, stands before nodig in the phrase iets nodig hebben. Zijn is possessive here, not the infinitive be. Nodig is an adjective complement, not a second verb. The noun is de goedkeuring, but zijn replaces the article.

Geef hem zijn rapport..scenario: Another person is holding a report belonging to a man. Tell them directly to give that man his report.

answers.explanation: The imperative geef starts the sentence and the understood subject you is omitted. Hem names the recipient, followed by what is given. Geef is the stem of geven. Hem is an object pronoun; zijn is possessive before rapport. They have different roles despite referring to the same person.

Zij legde de route uit..scenario: You are recounting a woman's help during an earlier journey. Explain that she explained the route.

answers.explanation: Legde is the finite past verb in second position. Uitleggen splits in this main clause, with uit after the object. Singular zij takes legde; plural zij would take legden. Uitleggen means explain. Uit alone is not a direction such as out of the room here.
Ze and zij refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

We hebben het voor haar gekocht..scenario: Someone asks who an item was bought for. Explain that your group bought it for a woman.

answers.text: We hebben het voor haar gekocht.
answers.explanation: Hebben is the finite second-position verb; gekocht closes the bracket. Het is what was bought and voor haar identifies the beneficiary. Kopen has the irregular participle gekocht. Haar follows the preposition voor; it is not possessive before a noun here.

answers.text: Wij hebben het voor haar gekocht.
answers.explanation: Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Kunt u dit verder uitleggen?.scenario: An explanation is not detailed enough for you. Politely ask the person, using formal address, to explain this further.

answers.explanation: The yes/no request begins with kunt, followed by u. Uitleggen stays together as the final infinitive after the modal. Kunt u retains t; the ordinary t-dropping rule before subject je does not apply to u. Kan u is also used in Belgium. Could expresses politeness here, not a Dutch past-tense form.
Kunt u and kan u are both standard; kan u is particularly common in Belgium. U keeps polite address and the action remains an infinitive.

answers.text: Zou u dit verder kunnen uitleggen?
answers.explanation: Zou u ... kunnen + infinitive phrases the same request more tentatively/politely. Kunnen is an infinitive after zou; the action also remains an infinitive. This is a present polite request, not a report about a past ability.

Ik zal de middelen toewijzen..scenario: Your team needs its available resources assigned to tasks. Say that you will allocate the resources.

answers.explanation: Zal is second and toewijzen is the final infinitive. The object de middelen stands inside the verb bracket. Middelen can mean resources or means; this project context selects resources. Toewijzen is separable, but remains joined after zal; Ik wijs de middelen toe uses the finite lexical verb.

Hij heeft gisteravond laat gewerkt..scenario: You are talking about a man's work yesterday evening. Explain that he worked late that evening.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. The other verb normally occurs toward the end. Heeft is second and gewerkt ends the perfect bracket. Gisteravond gives the day/evening, and laat narrows it to a late time. Werken forms the perfect with hebben. Heeft agrees with hij; gewerkt is the participle. This phrase order is natural, not a universal rule for all time expressions.
Werkte is simple past. The perfect has heeft ... gewerkt. Both fit the completed work yesterday evening.
The time gisteravond comes first, then heeft and subject hij. Laat still describes how late he worked.

Je zou het me moeten brengen..scenario: Another person has an item you need. Tell them that they should bring it to you, giving advice rather than a bare command.

answers.text: Je zou het me moeten brengen.
answers.english: You should bring it to me.
answers.explanation: Zou occupies second position. The object pronouns stand before the final modal-plus-infinitive group moeten brengen. Zou moeten gives a recommendation or expectation rather than an unconditional future promise. Moeten is an infinitive after zou; brengen is the lexical infinitive after moeten.

answers.text: Jij zou het me moeten brengen.
answers.english: You should bring it to me.
answers.explanation: Jij and je refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Ik ben aan het bellen..scenario: Someone asks what you are doing right now. Explain that you are making a phone call.

answers.explanation: Ben is second. Aan het + infinitive describes an action in progress; bellen is the infinitive, not another finite verb. Aan het is a fixed ongoing-action construction here. Ik bel can also mean I am calling; aan het explicitly foregrounds the action as ongoing.

Ik leg het later uit..scenario: Someone wants an explanation, but now is not a good time. Tell them you will explain it later.

answers.explanation: Leg is second. Uitleggen splits in the main clause, and uit appears after het later. Leg is present tense, but later and the promise context give future reference. Het is the object it, not an article before a noun here.

The time phrase and subject exchange main-clause positions around the finite verb. One whole constituent is first, the finite verb is second, and the subject follows it if time is first. The event and time are unchanged.

Een toekomst opbouwen vraagt werk..scenario: Someone hopes to build a future without much effort. Explain that building a future takes work.

answers.explanation: The whole phrase Een toekomst opbouwen is one subject constituent. Vraagt is second by constituent, although it is the fourth written word. The infinitive phrase acts as a singular subject, so vraagt has t. Opbouwen remains together inside that subject phrase; werk is an uncountable noun here.

Mijn voorstel is klaar..scenario: Your colleague asks about the proposal you were preparing. Tell them that your proposal is ready.

answers.explanation: Mijn voorstel is one subject constituent; is is the second constituent. Klaar says something about the subject. Klaar is a predicate adjective and receives no attributive -e ending here. Mijn replaces the article of het voorstel.

Kunt u dit afhandelen?.scenario: You need someone to deal with a matter and bring it to completion. Politely ask, using formal address, whether they can handle it.

answers.english: Could you take care of this?
answers.explanation: Kunt starts the yes/no request; u follows. Afhandelen remains one final infinitive after the modal. Afhandelen means deal with and bring to completion, especially a request or case. Kunt u is neutral polite written Dutch; kan u is also used in Belgian speech.

answers.english: Could you take care of this?
answers.explanation: Kunt u and kan u are both standard; kan u is particularly common in Belgium. U keeps polite address and the action remains an infinitive.

answers.english: Could you take care of this?
answers.explanation: Zou u ... kunnen + infinitive phrases the same request more tentatively/politely. Kunnen is an infinitive after zou; the action also remains an infinitive. This is a present polite request, not a report about a past ability.

Hij is bezig met het repareren van het l.scenario: A man is occupied with repairing a leak right now. Tell someone what he is busy doing.

answers.text: Hij is bezig met het repareren van het lek.
answers.explanation: Hij is first and is is second. Bezig describes his activity; the met-phrase specifies what keeps him occupied. Het repareren nominalizes the infinitive, so van het lek supplies what is repaired. This is not a second finite verb. Het lek uses het because lek is neuter as a noun.

answers.text: Hij is bezig het lek te repareren.
answers.english: He is busy fixing the leak.
answers.explanation: The verbal te-infinitive takes direct object het lek. The original uses the noun-like activity het repareren van het lek.

Mag ik iets voorstellen?.scenario: You have an idea to contribute to a discussion. Ask permission to suggest something.

answers.explanation: Mag starts the yes/no permission question. The infinitive voorstellen stays together at the end after iets. Mogen expresses permission here, not ability. Voorstellen means suggest in this context; it can mean introduce in a different context, so the object and scene matter.

Ik ben ziek..scenario: Someone asks why you cannot work as usual. Tell them that you are ill.

answers.explanation: Ik is first and ben is the second constituent. Ziek describes the subject rather than an object. Ben is the first-person present of zijn. Ziek is a predicate adjective, so no attributive -e ending is added. Ill describes illness here, not disgust.

Het netwerk heeft regelmatig onderhoud n.scenario: You are discussing the computer network's upkeep. Explain that it needs maintenance on a regular basis.

answers.text: Het netwerk heeft regelmatig onderhoud nodig.
answers.explanation: Het netwerk is one subject constituent and heeft is second. The thing needed comes before nodig in hebben ... nodig. Onderhoud is an uncountable het-noun. Regelmatig is an attributive adjective without -e before this indefinite neuter noun. No article is needed with uncountable onderhoud here.

Ik verkoop mijn oude laptop..scenario: Someone asks what you are doing with your old laptop. Tell them that you are selling it.

answers.explanation: Ik comes first and verkoop is second. Mijn oude laptop is the direct object being sold. Verkopen is inseparable; ver- is not a loose final particle. Oude takes -e inside this possessed noun phrase. The present describes a current sale offer.

Is het duidelijk?.scenario: You have just explained something to another person. Ask whether it is clear.

answers.explanation: The yes/no question starts with is, followed by its subject het. Duidelijk describes the explanation referred to by het. Het is a subject pronoun here, not an article before a noun. Duidelijk has no -e as a predicate adjective.

Kom opdagen..scenario: Someone has agreed to attend an event. Tell them directly to show up, without adding a new time or place.

answers.explanation: The command begins with kom; the understood subject you is omitted. Opdagen remains joined as the infinitive in komen opdagen. Komen opdagen means appear or show up for an expected event. It is not the main-clause split of one verb called komopdagen.

Deze investering is erg riskant..scenario: You are discussing a particular investment. Warn that this investment is very risky.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Deze investering occupies one first constituent. Is is second, and erg modifies the predicate adjective riskant. Investering is a de-word, so deze is the singular nearby demonstrative. Predicate riskant receives no -e; erg means very here, not bad.
Heel and erg both mean very as degree adverbs before this adjective/adverb. This changes the wording, not the stated degree or who the sentence describes.

Jij betaalt het haar..scenario: You are identifying who makes a payment to a woman. Tell the person you are addressing that they pay it to her.

answers.explanation: Jij is first and betaalt is second. Het refers to the amount paid; haar is the recipient. With this unstressed object pronoun, het can precede the recipient. Jij is the full subject form and can carry contrastive stress. Betaalt retains -t with a preceding jij. Haar is not possessive here because no possessed noun follows it.
Je and jij refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Ik ben een halfuur te vroeg voor de verg.scenario: You have arrived thirty minutes before the meeting starts. Explain that you are half an hour too early for it.

answers.text: Ik ben een halfuur te vroeg voor de vergadering.
answers.english: I'm half an hour too early for the meeting.
answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Ben is second after ik. Een halfuur specifies how much too early; voor de vergadering identifies the event. Te intensifies vroeg beyond the appropriate time, unlike gewoon vroeg. Halfuur and half uur are both accepted spellings for this duration; neither is the clock phrase half acht.

Hij heeft het voor ons gemaakt..scenario: Someone asks who an item was made for. Explain that a man made it for your group.

answers.text: Hij heeft het voor ons gemaakt.
answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. The other verb normally occurs toward the end. Heeft is second and gemaakt closes the perfect bracket. Het is the thing made; voor ons identifies its intended beneficiaries. For this making-something-for-someone sense, voor ons is natural. A bare recipient ons is not a general replacement for every for-phrase. Maken forms its perfect with hebben.

Geef deze map aan de manager..scenario: You are pointing to a particular folder. Tell someone to give this folder to the manager.

answers.text: Geef deze map aan de manager.
answers.english: Give this folder to the manager.
answers.explanation: Geef begins the command without an expressed subject. The object comes next; the aan-phrase specifies the recipient. Map is a de-word, so this folder is deze map. Aan marks the person receiving it; it does not mean on in this context.
The recipient can precede the object without aan. Map is a de-word, so attributive deze is correct.

Ik ben klaar voor mijn presentatie..scenario: Your presentation has not begun yet, but you are prepared. Explain that you are ready for your presentation.

answers.text: Ik ben klaar voor mijn presentatie.
answers.explanation: Ben is second. Klaar describes the subject, and voor mijn presentatie specifies what the readiness concerns. Klaar voor means ready for. Klaar alone can also mean finished; the added voor-phrase selects readiness here. Mijn is possessive before presentatie.

Schrijf je nu het verslag?.scenario: A colleague is at a desk. Ask whether they are writing the report right now.

answers.english: Are you writing the report now?
answers.explanation: The yes/no question starts with schrijf, then subject je. Nu marks the current time and het verslag is what is being written. Schrijft becomes schrijf before subject je in inversion. This t-dropping concerns je as subject, not a possessive je before a noun.

answers.english: Are you writing the report now?
answers.explanation: Jij and je refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Moet je me dat vóór de vergadering verte.scenario: Someone wants to tell you something before the meeting. Ask whether they have to tell you that before the meeting.

answers.text: Moet je me dat vóór de vergadering vertellen?
answers.english: Do you have to tell me that before the meeting?
answers.explanation: Moet starts the yes/no question. Vertellen is the final infinitive; the pronouns and time phrase fit between them. Moeten expresses necessity, not permission. The accent on vóór emphasizes before rather than for. Dat is the object that, not a subordinator introducing a clause.

answers.text: Moet jij me dat vóór de vergadering vertellen?
answers.english: Do you have to tell me that before the meeting?
answers.explanation: Jij and je refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Ik heb er één nodig..scenario: You are discussing forms and need just one of them. Explain that you need one, referring back to the forms without repeating the noun.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Heb is second. Er links the number één to the previously mentioned items, and nodig completes hebben ... nodig. Quantitative er does not mean there in this sentence. Één means one, with accents distinguishing it from the indefinite article een.

Grijp in..scenario: You see a situation in which someone needs to take action. Tell another person directly to intervene.

answers.explanation: Grijp begins the command; the understood subject you is omitted. In is the separated particle of ingrijpen. Ingrijpen means intervene in this scene. In is not a location or an instruction to grab a physical object.

Dat klinkt als een plan..scenario: Someone has suggested a workable plan. Respond that their suggestion sounds like a plan.

answers.explanation: Dat is the first subject constituent and klinkt is second. Als een plan supplies what the idea sounds like. Dat is a demonstrative subject, not a conjunction. Als means like in this comparison, not if introducing a subordinate clause.

Kunt u voorbeelden geven?.scenario: A person's explanation is too abstract. Politely ask them, using formal address, to give examples.

answers.explanation: Kunt begins the polite yes/no request, u follows, and geven stays as the final infinitive after voorbeelden. Voorbeelden is the plural of het voorbeeld. An indefinite plural noun does not require een. Kunt u retains -t, unlike ordinary inversion before je.
Kunt u and kan u are both standard; kan u is particularly common in Belgium. U keeps polite address and the action remains an infinitive.

Zou u ... kunnen + infinitive phrases the same request more tentatively/politely. Kunnen is an infinitive after zou; the action also remains an infinitive. This is a present polite request, not a report about a past ability.

Ze zijn weg..scenario: Some visitors have left and are no longer here. Tell someone that they are gone.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Ze is first and the finite present zijn is second. Weg describes their current absence. Ze is plural here because zijn is plural; singular she would use is. Weg means gone or away, not the noun de weg meaning road.
Zij and ze refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Kunt u een offerte opstellen?.scenario: You want a written price quotation from a supplier. Politely ask them to draw one up.

answers.english: Could you draw up a quotation?
answers.explanation: Kunt begins the request, followed by u. Opstellen is the joined infinitive at the end after een offerte. Offerte means a price quotation, not a quotation from a book. Opstellen means draft or draw up; it remains together after the modal.

answers.english: Could you draw up a quotation?
answers.explanation: Kunt u and kan u are both standard; kan u is particularly common in Belgium. U keeps polite address and the action remains an infinitive.

answers.text: Zou u een offerte kunnen opstellen?
answers.english: Could you draw up a quotation?
answers.explanation: Zou u ... kunnen + infinitive phrases the same request more tentatively/politely. Kunnen is an infinitive after zou; the action also remains an infinitive. This is a present polite request, not a report about a past ability.

Wij hebben haar onze diensten aangeboden.scenario: A colleague asks what your team offered a woman. Explain that your team offered her your services.

answers.text: Wij hebben haar onze diensten aangeboden.
answers.explanation: Hebben is second and aangeboden closes the perfect bracket. The recipient haar comes before the full object noun phrase onze diensten. Aanbieden has participle aangeboden, with ge between aan and boden. Onze agrees with plural diensten. Wij can emphasize our team.

answers.text: We hebben haar onze diensten aangeboden.
answers.explanation: We and wij refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Gebruik dit formulier..scenario: Someone is unsure which form to complete. Point to one and tell them to use this form.

answers.explanation: The command begins with gebruik and omits the understood subject you. Dit formulier is the direct object. Formulier is a het-word, so the nearby singular demonstrative is dit. Gebruik is the verb stem in this imperative.

We hebben een nieuwe strategie nodig..scenario: Your group's current approach is inadequate. Explain that you need a new strategy.

answers.text: We hebben een nieuwe strategie nodig.
answers.explanation: Hebben is second. The object noun phrase comes before nodig in the need construction. Strategie is a de-word. Its attributive adjective takes -e even after een: een nieuwe strategie. Compare the indefinite het-word pattern een nieuw plan.

answers.text: Wij hebben een nieuwe strategie nodig.
answers.explanation: Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Kunnen we hun vergaderruimte gebruiken?.scenario: Another team has a meeting room that your group would like to use. Ask whether your group can use their room.

answers.english: Can we use their meeting room?
answers.explanation: Kunnen begins the yes/no question, followed by we. Gebruiken is the final infinitive after the object. Kunnen agrees with plural we. Hun is possessive before vergaderruimte, not the subject of the sentence. The question can ask about practical possibility or permission in context.

answers.english: Can we use their meeting room?
answers.explanation: Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Dit is onze erfenis..scenario: You are showing something your group leaves behind for future generations. Describe it as your group's legacy.

answers.explanation: Dit is an independent demonstrative subject and is comes second. Onze erfenis identifies what this refers to. Erfenis is a de-word, so the possessive is onze. Independent dit does not need to agree with the identifying noun; attributive deze erfenis would be different.

Heb je je taak afgemaakt?.scenario: A colleague was responsible for a task. Ask whether they have finished their task.

answers.explanation: Heb begins the yes/no question. The first je is the subject; the second belongs to the object noun phrase. Afgemaakt closes the perfect bracket. The first je is the subject, so question-form hebt becomes heb: Heb je ...? The second je is possessive your before taak. Afmaken: maak ... af; perfect afgemaakt. For object it, use Heb je het al afgemaakt? Unstressed het normally comes early in the middle of the clause, before al and the participle.
Jij and je refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Ik zal haar agenda controleren..scenario: You need to check a woman's appointments. Say that you will check her calendar.

answers.explanation: Ik is the first constituent; zal is finite and second. Haar agenda stands between zal and the final infinitive controleren. Haar is possessive before agenda. Agenda means appointment diary/calendar here, unlike the meeting-item sense used earlier. Controleren is an inseparable verb and stays whole.

Laten we ons voorstel afronden..scenario: Your group has nearly finished a proposal. Suggest finalising your group's proposal together.

answers.explanation: Laten we introduces a joint suggestion. The object ons voorstel comes before final infinitive afronden. Voorstel is singular and takes het, so our proposal is ons voorstel. Afronden remains joined after laten; as a finite lexical verb it splits: We ronden het voorstel af.
Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.
Zullen we + infinitive offers the shared activity as a question. Laten we introduces it as a let’s-suggestion. Both fit proposing this joint activity; neither reports a completed event.

Ik had al naar kantoor gebeld..scenario: You are recounting a past request to phone the office. Explain that you had already called the office before that request.

answers.text: Ik had al naar kantoor gebeld.
answers.explanation: Had is finite and second; gebeld closes the past-perfect bracket. Al and naar kantoor occupy the middle of the clause. Had gebeld places the call before another past reference point. Al means already here. Naar kantoor bellen means phone the office, not physically travel there.

Ons project is uitdagend..scenario: Someone asks about the project your group is working on. Describe your project as challenging.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Ons project is one first constituent; is is second. Uitdagend is the predicate description of the project. Project is a het-word, so singular our project uses ons. Predicate uitdagend has no attributive -e. It means challenging in this context, not deliberately provocative.

Hij is bezig met het laden van de vracht.scenario: A man is occupied with putting goods into a truck right now. Explain what he is busy doing.

answers.text: Hij is bezig met het laden van de vrachtwagen.
answers.explanation: Hij comes first and is is second. The met-phrase identifies the ongoing activity described by bezig. Het laden is a noun-like infinitive. Van de vrachtwagen supplies what is being loaded in this version. Laden here means load goods, not charge a battery.

answers.text: Hij is bezig de vrachtwagen te laden.
answers.english: He is busy loading the truck.
answers.explanation: Bezig can introduce de vrachtwagen te laden. The truck remains the thing loaded; laden is an infinitive, not a finite verb.

Kun je me de toegangscode vertellen?.scenario: You need an access code. Ask a colleague, using informal address, to tell you the code.

answers.text: Kun je me de toegangscode vertellen?
answers.english: Can you tell me the access code?
answers.explanation: Kun begins the question, followed by subject je. Recipient me comes before the full object noun phrase, and vertellen is the final infinitive. Kun je is the inverted second-person form of kunnen; kan je is also valid. Vertellen means tell, not talk intransitively. Toegangscode is a de-word.

answers.text: Kun jij me de toegangscode vertellen?
answers.english: Can you tell me the access code?
answers.explanation: Jij and je refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

answers.text: Kan je me de toegangscode vertellen?
answers.english: Can you tell me the access code?
answers.explanation: Kun je and kan je are both standard forms of kunnen with subject je. The action still follows as an infinitive.

answers.text: Zou je me de toegangscode kunnen vertellen?
answers.english: Could you tell me the access code?
answers.explanation: Zou je ... kunnen + infinitive phrases the same request more tentatively/politely. Kunnen is an infinitive after zou; the action also remains an infinitive. This is a present polite request, not a report about a past ability.

Vind de ontbrekende documenten..scenario: Some documents are missing. Tell another person directly to find the missing documents.

answers.explanation: Vind begins the command without an expressed subject. The full noun phrase names what should be found. Vind is the stem of vinden; it has no extra -t in this imperative. Ontbrekende is an attributive participial adjective before definite plural documenten.

Kun je me de nieuwe veiligheidsregels ui.scenario: There are new safety rules you do not understand. Ask a colleague to explain those rules to you.

answers.text: Kun je me de nieuwe veiligheidsregels uitleggen?
answers.english: Can you explain the new safety rules to me?
answers.explanation: Kun starts the question. Recipient me precedes the full object phrase; uitleggen remains a joined final infinitive after the modal. Nieuwe takes -e before the definite plural veiligheidsregels. Uitleggen is separable when finite, but joined after kun. This requests an explanation, not permission to ignore rules.

answers.text: Kun jij me de nieuwe veiligheidsregels uitleggen?
answers.english: Can you explain the new safety rules to me?
answers.explanation: Jij and je refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

answers.text: Kan je me de nieuwe veiligheidsregels uitleggen?
answers.english: Can you explain the new safety rules to me?
answers.explanation: Kun je and kan je are both standard forms of kunnen with subject je. The action still follows as an infinitive.

answers.text: Zou je me de nieuwe veiligheidsregels kunnen uitleggen?
answers.english: Could you explain the new safety rules to me?
answers.explanation: Zou je ... kunnen + infinitive phrases the same request more tentatively/politely. Kunnen is an infinitive after zou; the action also remains an infinitive. This is a present polite request, not a report about a past ability.

Ze is goed in dingen uitleggen..scenario: A woman explains things well. Tell someone about her skill at explaining things.

answers.text: Ze is goed in dingen uitleggen.
answers.explanation: Ze precedes finite is. Goed describes her ability, and the in-phrase names the activity she does well. Goed in is the fixed combination for being skilled at something. Dingen uitleggen functions as an activity phrase after in; uitleggen is an infinitive and stays together.

answers.text: Zij is goed in dingen uitleggen.
answers.explanation: Zij and ze refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Praat er alsjeblieft met me over..scenario: Someone is keeping a concern to themselves. Politely ask them, using informal address, to talk with you about it.

answers.text: Praat er alsjeblieft met me over.
answers.english: Please talk with me about it.
answers.explanation: An instruction starts with the verb. Praat begins the command. Er and over refer to the topic, but are separated by alsjeblieft met me. Met me identifies the conversation partner. Er ... over together mean about it; er is not a location here. When adjacent, the pair is written erover. Alsjeblieft matches informal je-based conversation.

Het spijt me dit te moeten vragen..scenario: You have to ask someone an uncomfortable question. Express that you are sorry to have to ask it.

answers.text: Het spijt me dit te moeten vragen.
answers.english: I'm sorry to have to ask this.
answers.explanation: Het supplies the subject and spijt is finite and second. The infinitive clause dit te moeten vragen identifies the regretted necessity. Me is the object-form experiencer in het spijt me. Te belongs with moeten; vragen remains a bare infinitive after that modal. Dit is the thing asked.

Zij heeft me mijn badge teruggegeven..scenario: A woman has returned your badge to you. Tell someone what she gave back to you.

answers.text: Zij heeft me mijn badge teruggegeven.
answers.english: She gave me my badge back.
answers.explanation: Heeft is second and teruggegeven closes the perfect bracket. Recipient me comes before the full object noun phrase mijn badge. Teruggeven has the irregular participle teruggegeven, with ge inside the separable compound. Mijn is possessive before badge; me is recipient, not possessive.

answers.text: Ze heeft me mijn badge teruggegeven.
answers.english: She gave me my badge back.
answers.explanation: Ze and zij refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Breng dit pakket naar de receptie..scenario: You are pointing to a package that must go to reception. Tell someone to take this package there.

answers.text: Breng dit pakket naar de receptie.
answers.explanation: Breng starts the command and omits the understood subject. The object is followed by its destination phrase. Pakket is a het-word, so this package is dit pakket. Naar introduces the destination reception; it is not the person receiving something expressed with aan.

Wat is de agenda voor vanmiddag?.scenario: You are preparing for this afternoon's meeting. Ask what the agenda is for this afternoon.

answers.text: Wat is de agenda voor vanmiddag?
answers.english: What is the agenda for this afternoon?
answers.explanation: Wat is the first question constituent, followed by finite is and the subject noun phrase. Voor vanmiddag specifies which agenda is meant. Agenda means the planned meeting programme here, not an appointment diary. Vanmiddag is this afternoon; morgenmiddag would mean tomorrow afternoon.

Het product heeft een update nodig..scenario: A product is out of date. Explain that the product needs an update.

answers.text: Het product heeft een update nodig.
answers.explanation: Het product is one subject constituent and heeft is second. The required thing stands before nodig in heeft ... nodig. Product is a het-word; update is a borrowed de-noun. Heeft agrees with the singular product. Nodig is an adjective complement, not an extra verb.

Ik regel het..scenario: Someone has a problem that you can handle. Offer to take care of it.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Ik is first and finite regel is second. Het refers to the arrangement already mentioned. Regelen means arrange or take care of here. The present tense can express a near-future commitment in this context; it is not a claim that every Dutch present translates as will.
Ervoor refers back to the matter already discussed. Zorgen voor and regelen are different expressions that fit taking responsibility for this arrangement.

Kunt u een oplossing voor dit netwerkpro.scenario: You are speaking formally to a specialist about a network problem. Ask whether they can provide a solution to this problem.

answers.text: Kunt u een oplossing voor dit netwerkprobleem bieden?
answers.english: Could you provide a solution to this network problem?
answers.explanation: Kunt begins the polite request, then u. The complete solution noun phrase comes before final infinitive bieden. Voor dit netwerkprobleem modifies oplossing. Netwerkprobleem is a het-word and takes dit. Bieden is an infinitive after kunt; could expresses polite English, not Dutch past ability.

answers.text: Kan u een oplossing voor dit netwerkprobleem bieden?
answers.english: Could you provide a solution to this network problem?
answers.explanation: Kunt u and kan u are both standard; kan u is particularly common in Belgium. U keeps polite address and the action remains an infinitive.

answers.text: Zou u een oplossing voor dit netwerkprobleem kunnen bieden?
answers.english: Could you provide a solution to this network problem?
answers.explanation: Zou u ... kunnen + infinitive phrases the same request more tentatively/politely. Kunnen is an infinitive after zou; the action also remains an infinitive. This is a present polite request, not a report about a past ability.

Uw input is cruciaal..scenario: Someone you address formally doubts the value of their contribution. Explain that their input is crucial.

answers.explanation: Uw input forms the subject constituent and is is second. Cruciaal describes the importance of that contribution. Uw is the polite possessive. Input is a borrowed noun meaning contribution or information here, not a keyboard action. Predicate cruciaal has no attributive -e.

Ik wil volgende week naar de beurs gaan..scenario: A trade fair is taking place next week. Tell someone that you want to go to it next week.

answers.text: Ik wil volgende week naar de beurs gaan.
answers.english: I want to go to the trade fair next week.
answers.explanation: Wil is finite and second; gaan closes the modal bracket. The time and destination phrases stand between the modal and infinitive. Willen expresses desire, not certainty that the trip will happen. Beurs means trade fair in this scene, not stock exchange or scholarship. Naar marks the destination.

answers.text: Volgende week wil ik naar de beurs gaan.
answers.english: I want to go to the trade fair next week.
answers.explanation: The time phrase and subject exchange main-clause positions around the finite verb. One whole constituent is first, the finite verb is second, and the subject follows it if time is first. The event and time are unchanged.

Ik weeg het pakket..scenario: A colleague asks what you are doing with a package. Explain that you are weighing the package.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Ik occupies the first position and finite weeg the second. Het pakket is the thing whose weight is being measured. Wegen means physically weigh in this scene, not mentally consider. The finite form is weeg, with doubled ee; the infinitive is wegen.

Hoor je me?.scenario: You are testing an audio connection with someone. Ask whether they can hear you.

answers.explanation: The neutral yes/no question starts with hoor, then subject je. Me is the person being heard. Hoort becomes hoor before subject je in ordinary inversion. Horen is hearing, not deliberately listening as luisteren. Me is an object pronoun.
Jij and je refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Zijn team heeft het erg druk..scenario: A man leads a team that has a great deal to do. Tell someone that his team is very busy.

answers.text: Zijn team heeft het erg druk.
answers.explanation: Zijn team is one subject constituent and heeft is second. Het erg druk belongs to the fixed expression het druk hebben. Team is singular here, so heeft is used. Zijn means his before team, not the verb be. Het in het druk hebben is part of the idiom, not an article before druk.

answers.text: Zijn team heeft het heel druk.
answers.explanation: Heel and erg both mean very as degree adverbs before this adjective/adverb. This changes the wording, not the stated degree or who the sentence describes.

Ik kijk ernaar uit..scenario: An upcoming event has already been mentioned. Say that you are looking forward to it, without naming the event again.

answers.explanation: Ik is first and kijk is second. Ernaar refers to the anticipated event, while uit is the separated particle of uitkijken. Adjacent er and naar join as ernaar. Uit remains separate because it belongs to uitkijken, not the pronoun/preposition pair. This is anticipation, not physically looking outside.

Ik vind het niet erg..scenario: Someone is concerned that a proposal might bother you. Reassure them that you do not mind.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Vind is second. Het refers to the proposed action; niet erg states that you do not judge it troublesome. Vinden means consider or judge here, not locate a lost object. Erg means bad or bothersome in this expression; it is not the degree adverb very used before druk.

Hun ideeën zijn innovatief..scenario: You are discussing another group's ideas. Describe their ideas as innovative.

answers.explanation: Hun ideeën is one subject constituent, followed by finite zijn. Innovatief describes the ideas. Hun is possessive before the plural noun, not an independent subject. Plural ideeën takes zijn. The diaeresis separates the vowel sounds in ideeën; predicate innovatief has no -e.

Ik begin er meteen mee..scenario: A task has just been agreed. Tell your colleague you will begin working on it immediately.

answers.english: I'll get started on it right away.
answers.explanation: Ik comes first and begin is second. Er and mee refer back to the assignment; meteen can stand between them. Beginnen met means to start on something. When the object of met is replaced by er, met becomes mee: ermee. Er is not a place word here. Begin is the ik form; the present can express an immediate commitment.

answers.english: I'll get started on it right away.
answers.explanation: Meteen is fronted, then begin and ik. When er and mee are adjacent, write ermee as one word; in the original they surround meteen.

Zijn inspanningen werden erkend..scenario: You are recalling a man's work being acknowledged by others. Explain that his efforts were recognised, without naming who recognised them.

answers.explanation: The plural subject comes first, werden is second, and erkend closes the passive verb bracket. Zijn is possessive here. Inspanningen is plural, so the past passive auxiliary is werden, not werd. Erkennen has the participle erkend without ge- because it starts with the inseparable prefix er-. This is a past passive, not a perfect tense.

We hebben meer tijd nodig..scenario: Your group cannot finish within the time available. Explain that you need more time.

answers.explanation: We comes first and hebben is second; the required thing meer tijd precedes nodig. Iets nodig hebben means to need something. Tijd is an uncountable quantity here, so meer tijd needs no indefinite article. Meer expresses a greater amount, not another separate appointment.
Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Ze praten over de prijs..scenario: Some people are discussing how much something costs right now. Tell someone what they are talking about.

answers.explanation: Ze is the subject, praten is second, and over de prijs gives the topic. Praten over introduces the subject of a conversation. The plural verb praten makes ze mean they here. Prijs means the amount charged in this scenario, not an award. De prijs uses de.
Zij and ze refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Goed gedaan..scenario: Someone has completed a task successfully. Congratulate them with a short expression meaning well done.

answers.explanation: This conventional praise expression has no finite verb. It is a natural short utterance; a full clause would be Dat heb je goed gedaan. Gedaan is the irregular participle of doen. Goed tells how the task was done. The omitted subject and auxiliary are understood from the completed action; the fragment is a complete praise speech act.
The full clause makes the successful action explicit. Dat is fronted as object, so auxiliary heb precedes subject je.

Zij stuurde de foto's naar ons..scenario: A woman sent photos to your group earlier. Tell someone what she sent to you.

answers.text: Zij stuurde de foto's naar ons.
answers.english: She sent the photos to us.
answers.explanation: Zij comes first and stuurde is second; the photos precede the recipient naar ons. Stuurde is the singular simple past of sturen. Naar marks the destination/recipient after sturen. Ons is an object pronoun after a preposition. Foto has the plural foto’s with an apostrophe to preserve the vowel sound.

answers.text: Ze stuurde de foto's naar ons.
answers.english: She sent the photos to us.
answers.explanation: Ze and zij refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Ik weet het nog niet zeker..scenario: Someone asks whether you are certain about a matter already discussed. Explain that you are not sure yet.

answers.text: Ik weet het nog niet zeker.
answers.explanation: Ik comes first and weet is second; het is followed by nog niet and zeker. Weten has the ik form weet. Het refers to the answer or decision. Nog niet means not yet, indicating that certainty may come later. Zeker expresses certainty; the whole expression is idiomatic.

Wat is het addertje onder het gras?.scenario: An offer seems unusually attractive. Ask what hidden disadvantage or catch there is.

answers.text: Wat is het addertje onder het gras?
answers.explanation: Wat asks for the hidden drawback, is is second, and the subject follows it. Een addertje onder het gras is an idiom for a concealed problem. Addertje is a diminutive and takes het. In this expression gras is used with het. The phrase is not a warning about a literal animal in this scenario.

Hij sprak met de manager..scenario: You are recounting a man's earlier conversation. Explain that he spoke with the manager.

answers.explanation: Hij comes first and sprak is second; met de manager names the conversation partner. Sprak is the irregular singular simple past of spreken; the plural is spraken. Met introduces the person spoken with, while over introduces a topic. Manager is a de-word.

Laten we taken delegeren..scenario: Your group has too much work concentrated on a few people. Suggest delegating tasks.

answers.explanation: The shared suggestion begins with Laten we; taken stands before the final infinitive delegeren. Laten we + infinitive proposes a joint action. Taken is the plural of de taak; the long vowel is spelled with one a in the open syllable of taken. An indefinite plural does not use een.
Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.
Zullen we + infinitive offers the shared activity as a question. Laten we introduces it as a let’s-suggestion. Both fit proposing this joint activity; neither reports a completed event.

Hij voltooide zijn taak..scenario: You are recounting a man's completed work. Explain that he finished his task.
