answers.explanation: Hij comes first and voltooide is second; zijn taak is the object. Voltooide is the singular simple past of voltooien. Zijn is possessive before de taak. This is a simple past clause, unlike Hij heeft zijn taak voltooid, which uses a perfect auxiliary and participle.
Heeft ... voltooid is perfect. Voltooid is the participle; voltooide is finite simple past.

Wie heeft de leiding?.scenario: You need to find the person responsible for leading an activity. Ask who is in charge.

answers.explanation: Wie itself is the subject. Heeft follows it; there is no extra subject pronoun after the verb. De leiding hebben means to be in charge. Heeft is the usual singular verb form in this question. Leiding refers to leadership here rather than a physical pipe.

Stuur het ondertekende contract naar hem.scenario: You have a signed contract that must reach a man. Tell someone to send the signed contract to him.

answers.text: Stuur het ondertekende contract naar hem.
answers.english: Send the signed contract to him.
answers.explanation: The instruction begins with the imperative Stuur, followed by the object and naar hem. An ordinary imperative uses the stem stuur. Contract is a het-word; after definite het the attributive participle receives -e: ondertekende. Ondertekenen is inseparable, with participle ondertekend. Hem is the object form after naar.

Ik moet een oplossing voor deze lekkage.scenario: You are dealing with a particular leak. Explain that you have to find a solution to this leak.

answers.text: Ik moet een oplossing voor deze lekkage vinden.
answers.english: I have to find a solution to this leak.
answers.explanation: Ik comes first and moet is second. The whole object phrase stands before the final infinitive vinden. Moeten expresses necessity; the main action is the infinitive vinden, without te. Oplossing is a de-word but uses een when indefinite. Voor introduces the problem requiring a solution. Deze agrees with de lekkage.

Ik ben hier om advies te vragen..scenario: Someone asks why you have come here. Explain that you are here to ask for advice.

answers.text: Ik ben hier om advies te vragen.
answers.english: I'm here to ask for advice.
answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Ik is first and ben second; hier gives the place and om advies te vragen gives the purpose. Om ... te + infinitive expresses purpose. Advies vragen takes advies as a direct object; Dutch does not insert voor in this expression. Advies is uncountable here and needs no een.

Ik ben vandaag druk bezig met de plannin.scenario: A colleague asks what is occupying you today. Explain that you are busy with the planning today.

answers.text: Ik ben vandaag druk bezig met de planning.
answers.english: I'm busy with the planning today.
answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Ik is first and ben second; vandaag gives the time, followed by druk bezig and met de planning. Druk bezig zijn met means to be busy with an activity. This expanded wording is natural in Belgium as well as the Netherlands. Planning is a de-word. Met introduces the activity occupying you.

answers.text: Vandaag ben ik druk bezig met de planning.
answers.english: I'm busy with the planning today.
answers.explanation: The time phrase and subject exchange main-clause positions around the finite verb. One whole constituent is first, the finite verb is second, and the subject follows it if time is first. The event and time are unchanged.

Luister goed..scenario: Someone needs to pay close attention to spoken information. Tell them directly to listen carefully.

answers.explanation: The instruction begins with Luister; goed describes how to listen. The understood subject is the person addressed. The ordinary imperative is the stem luister, without -t. Goed is an adverb here, so it has no adjective -e ending. Luisteren is paying attention to sounds; horen is perceiving them.

We hebben hun input vóór vrijdag nodig..scenario: Your group needs another group's input before Friday. Tell a colleague what you need and when you need it.

answers.text: We hebben hun input vóór vrijdag nodig.
answers.english: We need their input before Friday.
answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. We is first and hebben second; the object and deadline precede nodig. Hun is possessive before input, not an object pronoun in this use. Iets nodig hebben means to need something. Vóór emphasizes before rather than for. Dutch weekdays are lowercase.

answers.text: Wij hebben hun input vóór vrijdag nodig.
answers.english: We need their input before Friday.
answers.explanation: Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

answers.text: Vóór vrijdag hebben we hun input nodig.
answers.english: We need their input before Friday.
answers.explanation: The time phrase and subject exchange main-clause positions around the finite verb. One whole constituent is first, the finite verb is second, and the subject follows it if time is first. The event and time are unchanged.

Ik wacht op een telefoontje..scenario: Someone asks why you are keeping your phone close. Explain that you are waiting for a phone call.

answers.english: I'm waiting for a phone call.
answers.explanation: Ik comes first and wacht is second; op een telefoontje completes what you are waiting for. Wachten op is a fixed combination. Telefoontje means phone call here, not a miniature telephone. The diminutive has het as its definite article; een does not show noun gender.

Ze oefenen hun vaardigheden..scenario: Several people are improving their abilities through practice. Describe them as practising their skills.

answers.explanation: Ze comes first and oefenen is second; hun vaardigheden is the direct object. The plural verb oefenen makes ze mean they. Hun is possessive before the plural vaardigheden. De vaardigheid has the plural vaardigheden; oefenen can take the skill as a direct object.
Zij and ze refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Kunnen we deze deal sluiten?.scenario: Your group is considering finalising an agreement. Ask whether you can close this deal.

answers.explanation: The yes/no question begins with Kunnen, then we, the object, and the final infinitive sluiten. Kunnen agrees with plural we. De deal takes deze. Een deal sluiten means to conclude an agreement here, not to close a physical door. After kunnen use the infinitive without te.
Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Laten we de presentatie starten..scenario: Your group is ready to begin a presentation. Suggest starting the presentation together.

answers.explanation: Laten we introduces the shared proposal; the object precedes the final infinitive starten. De presentatie uses de. Starten is an infinitive after laten. The plural we includes the speaker and the people addressed in the proposed action.
Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.
Zullen we + infinitive offers the shared activity as a question. Laten we introduces it as a let’s-suggestion. Both fit proposing this joint activity; neither reports a completed event.

Dit is onze gedeelde visie..scenario: You are describing a vision agreed by your group. Identify it as your shared vision.

answers.explanation: Independent Dit is the subject, is is second, and onze gedeelde visie identifies what Dit refers to. Dit used on its own need not agree with de visie. Before de visie, our is onze. Gedeelde is an attributive participle used like an adjective; it receives -e in this definite possessive noun phrase.

Hoe gaat het met je werk?.scenario: You meet a friend and want to know how their work is going. Ask about their work.

answers.text: Hoe gaat het met je werk?
answers.explanation: Hoe comes first, gaat is second, and het follows as the grammatical subject. Met je werk gives the topic. In Hoe gaat het met ...?, het is the subject of gaat. Je is possessive before werk, so it does not trigger the inversion rule that removes -t when subject jij/je follows its verb. Het werk is a het-word.

Geef de reservebatterij aan de technicus.scenario: A technician needs a spare battery. Tell someone to give the spare battery to the technician.

answers.text: Geef de reservebatterij aan de technicus.
answers.english: Give the spare battery to the technician.
answers.explanation: An instruction starts with the verb. The instruction starts with Geef, then names the item and its recipient with aan. Geef is the stem and ordinary imperative of geven. Reservebatterij is one compound word and takes de from its head batterij. Aan introduces the receiver. De technicus names the professional receiving the battery.

answers.english: Give the technician the spare battery.
answers.explanation: The recipient precedes the direct object without aan. Geef is the imperative stem, with no subject pronoun.

Het spijt me dat te horen..scenario: Someone has told you bad news. Express that you are sorry to hear that.

answers.text: Het spijt me dat te horen.
answers.explanation: Het comes first, spijt is second, and me names the person who feels sorry. Dat is the object of horen in the infinitive phrase. Het spijt me is an idiomatic sympathy or regret expression. Here dat means that news, not a conjunction introducing a finite clause. Te horen uses an infinitive; me is an object pronoun.

Hij heeft ons verteld dat de trein vertr.scenario: A man informed your group that the train is delayed. Tell someone what he told you, keeping the train's delay as current information.

answers.text: Hij heeft ons verteld dat de trein vertraging heeft.
answers.english: He told us that the train is delayed.
answers.explanation: Hij heeft starts the main clause. Ons is the recipient; verteld precedes the full content clause. Inside that dat-clause, the finite verb heeft comes last. Vertellen uses hebben in the perfect and the inseparable participle verteld, without ge-. Ons is the recipient pronoun. Vertraging hebben means to be delayed. A full content clause can follow the main clause’s participle.

Wat is de snelheid?.scenario: You are discussing how fast something is moving. Ask what its speed is.

answers.explanation: Wat asks for a value; is is second and de snelheid follows it as the subject. Snelheid is a de-word. The suffix -heid forms an abstract noun from snel. The question asks about speed, not the time at which something happens.

Vind het antwoord in de handleiding..scenario: Someone needs a particular answer. Tell them to find the answer in the manual.

answers.text: Vind het antwoord in de handleiding.
answers.english: Find the answer in the manual.
answers.explanation: An instruction starts with the verb. The instruction begins with Vind, followed by the object and the location where the answer can be found. Vind is the stem of vinden and an ordinary imperative. Antwoord is a het-word; handleiding is a de-word. In introduces the source location.

Ik stuur mijn e-mail..scenario: You are ready to send an email you wrote. Tell someone that you will send your email.

answers.explanation: Ik comes first and stuur is second; mijn e-mail is the object. Sturen has the ik form stuur. Mijn is possessive and replaces an article before e-mail. The present can express an immediate intention; no zal is required. E-mail retains its hyphen.

Acteren is een veeleisend beroep..scenario: Someone asks about acting as a career. Describe it as a demanding profession.

answers.explanation: The infinitive Acteren functions as the subject; is is second. The profession is described in the predicate. An infinitive used as an activity subject normally takes a singular verb. Beroep is a het-word, so after indefinite een the adjective has no -e: veeleisend beroep. With definite het: het veeleisende beroep.

Ik heb je de geleende sleutel teruggegev.scenario: You borrowed a key from the person you are addressing and have returned it. Tell them what you gave back.

answers.text: Ik heb je de geleende sleutel teruggegeven.
answers.english: I returned the borrowed key to you.
answers.explanation: Ik comes first and heb second. The short recipient pronoun je precedes the full noun object; teruggegeven closes the perfect verb bracket. Teruggeven is separable: ik geef terug; in the participle ge- goes between terug and geven. Geven has the irregular participle gegeven. Je is an object pronoun here. Geleende is an attributive participle before de sleutel.

Ze weet waar ze het over heeft..scenario: A woman speaks knowledgeably about a topic. Explain that she knows what she is talking about.

answers.text: Ze weet waar ze het over heeft.
answers.english: She knows what she is talking about.
answers.explanation: Ze weet starts the main clause. In the embedded clause, waar comes first, then ze het over, and the finite verb heeft comes last. Het ergens over hebben means to talk about something. Waar ... over asks about that topic and can be separated around the other clause words. The singular weet and heeft make ze mean she here.

answers.text: Zij weet waar ze het over heeft.
answers.english: She knows what she is talking about.
answers.explanation: Zij and ze refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Kunt u dat toelichten?.scenario: A point needs more explanation. Politely ask the person, using formal address, to clarify that in more detail.

answers.english: Could you explain that in more detail?
answers.explanation: The polite yes/no request starts with Kunt, followed by u, dat, and the final infinitive toelichten. Kunt u is a standard polite form; kan u is also standard, especially in Belgium. Toelichten means explain or clarify and is separable in a finite statement: u licht dat toe. After a modal the infinitive stays together.

answers.english: Could you explain that in more detail?
answers.explanation: Kunt u and kan u are both standard; kan u is particularly common in Belgium. U keeps polite address and the action remains an infinitive.

answers.english: Could you explain that in more detail?
answers.explanation: Zou u ... kunnen + infinitive phrases the same request more tentatively/politely. Kunnen is an infinitive after zou; the action also remains an infinitive. This is a present polite request, not a report about a past ability.

Wat is er over?.scenario: Some things have been used up. Ask what remains, without assuming a particular quantity is left.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Wat asks which thing remains; is follows it. Er supports the presentation of a remainder, while over means left/remaining. Over zijn means to be left over. Wat is the grammatical question subject. Er is not replacing a met/op object in this sentence and is not translated literally as there in the natural English question.

Zijn tijd is gekomen..scenario: A man now has the opportunity he has been waiting for. Tell someone that his time has come, in this positive opportunity sense.

answers.explanation: The whole phrase Zijn tijd is the subject; is is second and gekomen closes the perfect bracket. Zijn is possessive before tijd, not an infinitive. In this personal scenario it means his. Komen uses zijn in the perfect: is gekomen. The expression signals that a person’s opportunity has arrived; other contexts can give it a more ominous meaning.

Ik wil de nieuwe scanner gebruiken..scenario: A new scanner is available. Explain that you want to use the new scanner.

answers.text: Ik wil de nieuwe scanner gebruiken.
answers.english: I want to use the new scanner.
answers.explanation: Ik comes first and wil is second; the object stands before the final infinitive gebruiken. Willen expresses desire rather than future will. After wil use an infinitive without te. De scanner takes the attributive adjective nieuwe. Gebruiken is inseparable.

Dat is een goed punt..scenario: Someone makes a useful observation during a discussion. Respond that it is a good point.

answers.explanation: Dat comes first and is second; een goed punt identifies the observation as useful. Punt in the observation sense is a het-word. After indefinite een the adjective has no -e: goed punt. Dat stands independently and points to the previous remark.

Kunnen ze hem leren hoe hij de machine m.scenario: Some experienced people could train a man. Ask whether they can teach him how to operate the machine.

answers.text: Kunnen ze hem leren hoe hij de machine moet bedienen?
answers.english: Can they teach him how to operate the machine?
answers.explanation: Kunnen starts the question. The main infinitive leren precedes the embedded how-clause. Inside that clause, hij de machine comes before the final verb group moet bedienen. Ze is plural because of kunnen. Leren means teach when someone is its recipient. Hem is the object form. Moet is finite inside the embedded clause; bedienen is an infinitive without te. The order bedienen moet is also possible in a subordinate verb group.

answers.text: Kunnen zij hem leren hoe hij de machine moet bedienen?
answers.english: Can they teach him how to operate the machine?
answers.explanation: Zij and ze refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

We plannen ons budget..scenario: Your team is deciding how to use its available money. Speaking for the team, explain that you are planning your budget.

answers.explanation: We comes first and plannen is second; ons budget is the object. Ons and onze both mean our. Budget is singular and takes het, so use ons budget. Use onze before a singular de-word (onze auto) and every plural (onze budgetten). The number of owners does not decide the ending. We plannen is the plural present of plannen; Ik plande is simple past and We hebben gepland is perfect.

answers.text: We zijn ons budget aan het plannen.
answers.explanation: Zijn + aan het + infinitive explicitly marks ongoing planning. Budget is a singular het-word, so the possessive stays ons.
Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Ze hebben me geleerd hoe ik de veilighei.scenario: Some people taught you to fasten a safety belt. Explain what they taught you how to do.

answers.text: Ze hebben me geleerd hoe ik de veiligheidsriem moet vastmaken.
answers.english: They taught me how to fasten the safety belt.
answers.explanation: Ze hebben begins the main clause. Me precedes geleerd; the embedded how-clause follows the participle. Its verb group moet vastmaken comes after ik and the object. Hebben geleerd is a perfect. Me is the recipient, so leren means teach. Vastmaken is separable in a finite simple clause but stays whole as an infinitive after moet. Vastmaken moet is also a possible subordinate verb order.

answers.text: Zij hebben me geleerd hoe ik de veiligheidsriem moet vastmaken.
answers.english: They taught me how to fasten the safety belt.
answers.explanation: Zij and ze refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Help ze met het opruimen..scenario: Some people are tidying up and need assistance. Tell another person to help them with that activity.

answers.english: Help them with the tidying up.
answers.explanation: An instruction starts with the verb. Help begins the instruction. Ze is its object; met het opruimen names the activity requiring help. Ze can be an unstressed plural object pronoun as well as a subject pronoun in other clauses. Het opruimen is an infinitive used as an activity noun. Opruimen is separable in a finite clause: zij ruimen op.

Wat is ons geheime wapen?.scenario: You are discussing a special strength that gives your group an advantage. Ask what your group's secret weapon is, figuratively.

answers.explanation: Wat asks which advantage the team has; is is second and the subject phrase follows. Wapen is a singular het-word, so our is ons. After possessive ons, the attributive adjective takes -e: geheime. Geheime wapen is figurative here, referring to a special strength rather than a physical weapon.

Wij zijn te laat..scenario: Your group has arrived after the agreed time. Speaking for the group, explain that you are late.

answers.explanation: Wij comes first and plural zijn is second; te laat describes being beyond the expected time. Wij is the stressed form of we. Te before laat means too, not the infinitive marker te. Zijn agrees with the plural subject. Laat is predicative and has no adjective ending.
We and wij refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Verkoop de oude printer aan hem..scenario: A man wants to buy an old printer that your colleague can sell. Tell your colleague directly to sell the old printer to him.

answers.text: Verkoop de oude printer aan hem.
answers.english: Sell the old printer to him.
answers.explanation: An instruction starts with the verb. Verkoop starts the instruction; the object precedes the recipient aan hem. Verkopen is inseparable: verkoop, verkocht, heeft verkocht. Verkoop is the imperative stem. Je in Verkoop je auto means your; Verkoop je de auto? instead has subject je and asks are you selling? Aan introduces the buyer; te introduces an infinitive, not a buyer. Naar also occurs in non-movement expressions such as luisteren naar, so it is not simply a movement-only word.
The recipient can be an indirect object before the full noun object, without aan. Verkoop is the imperative of inseparable verkopen.

Zijn training was effectief..scenario: You are evaluating training a man received earlier. Explain that his training was effective.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Zijn training is the first constituent; was is second and effectief describes the training. Zijn is possessive. Was is the singular past of zijn. Effectief is predicative after was and receives no attributive -e. The sentence evaluates the training result, not the trainer’s physical fitness.

Een bedrijf runnen is moeilijk..scenario: Someone asks how hard it is to operate a business. Explain that running a business is difficult.

answers.explanation: The entire infinitive phrase Een bedrijf runnen is the first constituent. Is is second even though several words precede it. Runnen is a borrowed Dutch verb meaning manage or operate. The whole activity phrase acts as a singular subject. Bedrijf is a het-word but takes een when indefinite. Moeilijk is predicative and has no -e.

Kun je de uitnodiging voor me schrijven?.scenario: You need an invitation written. Ask a colleague informally to write the invitation for you.

answers.text: Kun je de uitnodiging voor me schrijven?
answers.english: Can you write the invitation for me?
answers.explanation: Kun starts the question, followed by subject je, the object and beneficiary; schrijven is final. In this question je is the subject following kun. Kun je is the normal form of kunnen with subject inversion. Me after voor is an object pronoun naming the beneficiary. This is different from possessive je inside a noun phrase.

answers.text: Kun jij de uitnodiging voor me schrijven?
answers.english: Can you write the invitation for me?
answers.explanation: Jij and je refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

answers.text: Kan je de uitnodiging voor me schrijven?
answers.english: Can you write the invitation for me?
answers.explanation: Kun je and kan je are both standard forms of kunnen with subject je. The action still follows as an infinitive.

answers.text: Zou je de uitnodiging voor me kunnen schrijven?
answers.english: Could you write the invitation for me?
answers.explanation: Zou je ... kunnen + infinitive phrases the same request more tentatively/politely. Kunnen is an infinitive after zou; the action also remains an infinitive. This is a present polite request, not a report about a past ability.

De economie groeit..scenario: Someone asks about the current economy. Explain that it is growing.

answers.explanation: De economie is the first constituent; groeit is the finite second-position verb. Groeien has the singular third-person present groeit. Economie is a singular de-word. Groeien is intransitive in this use, so it does not require a direct object.

De vergadering is geannuleerd..scenario: A meeting was scheduled, but its cancellation is now confirmed. Tell someone that the meeting has been cancelled.

answers.explanation: De vergadering comes first, is is second, and geannuleerd closes the verb bracket. Annuleren has participle geannuleerd. Is geannuleerd presents the completed passive cancellation or resulting cancelled state. It does not say who cancelled it. Wordt geannuleerd would describe an ongoing or scheduled cancellation.

Ze zijn van plan om laat te blijven..scenario: Some people intend to remain late, but have not done so yet. Explain their plan.

answers.text: Ze zijn van plan om laat te blijven.
answers.explanation: Ze comes first and zijn is second. Van plan expresses an intention; om laat te blijven explains the intended action. Van plan zijn om ... te + infinitive means to intend to do something. The plural zijn makes ze mean they. Laat describes the time until which they remain; blijven is an infinitive.

answers.text: Zij zijn van plan om laat te blijven.
answers.explanation: Zij and ze refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Ben je nu beschikbaar?.scenario: You need a colleague's attention now. Ask informally whether they are available at this moment.

answers.explanation: Ben begins the yes/no question; je is the subject, followed by nu and beschikbaar. Zijn has the inverted informal form ben je, corresponding to statement je bent. Beschikbaar is predicative, without -e, and means available for use or help in this scenario.
Jij and je refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

We denken erover om het menu te verander.scenario: Your group is considering a different menu, without having decided. Explain that you are thinking about changing the menu.

answers.text: We denken erover om het menu te veranderen.
answers.english: We're thinking about changing the menu.
answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. The other verb normally occurs toward the end. We is first and denken second. Erover anticipates the action explained by om het menu te veranderen. Denken over becomes erover when its topic is represented pronominally. The following om ... te phrase states the contemplated action. Menu is a het-word. Veranderen is inseparable.

answers.text: Wij denken erover om het menu te veranderen.
answers.english: We're thinking about changing the menu.
answers.explanation: Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Vertel ons erover..scenario: Someone knows about an event your group wants to hear about. Tell that person to tell your group about it.

answers.explanation: An instruction starts with the verb. Vertel starts the instruction, then ons names the listeners and erover refers to the previously mentioned experience. Vertellen has the imperative vertel. Erover combines er and over, referring to a thing or topic. Ons is an object/recipient pronoun, not a subject.
Aan ons makes the recipient explicit. Erover refers to the topic already mentioned; do not replace it with a literal location.

Ik waardeer je advies..scenario: Someone has given you advice. Explain that you appreciate their advice, using informal address.

answers.explanation: Ik comes first and waardeer is second; je advies is the direct object. Waarderen has the ik form waardeer. Je is possessive before advies, not the subject. Advies is uncountable here and needs no plural or indefinite article.

Onze klanten zijn belangrijk..scenario: A colleague asks how your group views its customers. Explain that your customers are important.

answers.explanation: Onze klanten is the first constituent, zijn is second, and belangrijk describes the plural subject. Klanten is plural, so our is onze regardless of the noun’s singular article. The plural subject requires zijn. Belangrijk is predicative and has no -e ending.

Ik had de brief al gestuurd..scenario: You are recalling a past reminder to send a letter. Explain that you had already sent the letter before that reminder.

answers.text: Ik had de brief al gestuurd.
answers.explanation: Ik comes first and had is second. De brief and al stand before the final participle gestuurd. Had + past participle forms the past perfect, describing an action completed before another past reference point. Sturen uses hebben, whose singular past is had. Al means already.

Ik heb er drie..scenario: You are discussing spare keys. Explain that you have three of them, referring back to the keys without repeating the noun.

answers.explanation: Ik comes first and heb is second; quantitative er stands before the number drie. Er refers to a previously named plural item, here spare keys. It is quantitative rather than a place word. When an indefinite countable noun is omitted after a number, er supplies that reference.

Het team heeft de deadline ondanks de st.scenario: A malfunction threatened the schedule, but the team met its deadline. Explain both the success and the obstacle it overcame.

answers.text: Het team heeft de deadline ondanks de storing gehaald.
answers.english: The team met the deadline despite the malfunction.
answers.explanation: Het team is first and heeft second. The object and concession phrase precede the final participle gehaald. Een deadline halen means to meet a deadline. Team is grammatically singular, requiring heeft. Ondanks introduces an obstacle that did not prevent success. Storing is a de-word; halen uses participle gehaald.

Ik ben daar niet zeker van..scenario: Someone asks whether you are certain about a claim. Explain that you are not sure about that claim.

answers.text: Ik ben daar niet zeker van.
answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Ik is first and ben second; daar and van can be separated by niet zeker. Zeker zijn van means to be sure of something. Daar ... van refers back to the claim; it is a pronominal adverb, not a literal location. Niet negates the certainty.

Hij was niet aan het bureau..scenario: You are recounting where a man was at an earlier moment. Explain that he was not at the desk, rather than describing an ongoing activity.

answers.text: Hij was niet aan het bureau.
answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Hij is first and was second; niet negates presence at the following desk location. Was is singular past of zijn. Bureau in the desk sense is a het-word. Aan het bureau locates the person at the desk; it is not the aan het + infinitive progressive construction.

Ik probeer de kapotte lamp te repareren..scenario: A lamp is broken and you are attempting a repair. Explain that you are trying to repair the broken lamp, without claiming success yet.

answers.text: Ik probeer de kapotte lamp te repareren.
answers.english: I'm trying to repair the broken lamp.
answers.explanation: Ik comes first and probeer second; the object stands before te repareren. Proberen takes a te-infinitive, unlike modal kunnen. Lamp is a de-word; the adjective is kapotte. Repareren is a whole infinitive, with te placed directly before it.

Dit programma is makkelijk te leren..scenario: Someone asks how difficult a particular program is to learn. Explain that this program is easy to learn.

answers.text: Dit programma is makkelijk te leren.
answers.english: This program is easy to learn.
answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. The other verb normally occurs toward the end. Dit programma is the first constituent, is is second, and makkelijk te leren describes it. Programma is a het-word, so attributive this is dit. Makkelijk is predicative and has no -e. Te leren specifies the action that is easy; the program is what is learned, not the learner.

answers.text: Dit programma is gemakkelijk te leren.
answers.english: This program is easy to learn.
answers.explanation: Makkelijk and gemakkelijk both mean easy here. Both are predicate adjectives and have no attributive -e in this construction.

Wat is beter: repareren of vervangen?.scenario: Something is broken and you are comparing two options. Ask which is better: repairing it or replacing it.

answers.text: Wat is beter: repareren of vervangen?
answers.explanation: Wat is beter forms the main question. After the colon, two infinitives name the alternatives being compared. Beter is the irregular comparative of goed. Of joins alternatives. Repareren and vervangen name activities as infinitives; betterer is not a Dutch comparative form.

Het overleg is erg kort..scenario: Someone asks about the duration of a discussion. Explain that the discussion is very short.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Het overleg is first and is second; erg modifies the adjective kort. Overleg is a het-word. Kort describes duration here, not physical length. Erg means very as a degree adverb; kort is predicative and receives no -e.
Heel and erg both mean very as degree adverbs before this adjective/adverb. This changes the wording, not the stated degree or who the sentence describes.

We hadden de winkel al gesloten..scenario: You are recalling a customer's arrival after closing time. Explain that your group had already closed the shop before that arrival.

answers.text: We hadden de winkel al gesloten.
answers.explanation: We is first and hadden second. The object and al precede the participle gesloten. Hadden is the plural past of hebben. Hadden gesloten is a past perfect, locating closure before the customer’s past arrival. Sluiten has irregular participle gesloten. The shop is the object, so the auxiliary is hebben.

answers.text: Wij hadden de winkel al gesloten.
answers.explanation: Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Hun voorstel werd geaccepteerd..scenario: You are recounting the outcome of another group's proposal. Explain that their proposal was accepted, without naming who accepted it.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. The other verb normally occurs toward the end. Hun voorstel is the first constituent; werd is second and geaccepteerd closes the passive bracket. Voorstel is grammatically singular even though hun names plural possessors, so use werd. Hun is possessive. Accepteren has participle geaccepteerd. This is a past passive, not a completed passive with is.

Heb je me het nieuwe ontwerp laten zien?.scenario: A colleague may already have shown you a new design. Ask whether they have shown it to you.

answers.text: Heb je me het nieuwe ontwerp laten zien?
answers.english: Have you shown me the new design?
answers.explanation: Heb begins the perfect question, then je, me and the object; laten zien forms the final verb group. Laten zien means show. In the perfect with a following infinitive, laten is a replacing infinitive rather than the participle gelaten. Zien remains an infinitive too. Heb je lacks -t because subject je follows the verb. Ontwerp is a het-word, but definite het gives nieuwe an -e.

answers.text: Heb jij me het nieuwe ontwerp laten zien?
answers.english: Have you shown me the new design?
answers.explanation: Jij and je refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Doe dit voordat je vertrekt..scenario: Someone is about to leave, but a task must be done first. Tell them to do this before leaving.

answers.explanation: Doe begins the main instruction and dit is its object. In the voordat-clause, subject je precedes the final finite verb vertrekt. Doe is the imperative of doen. Dit points independently to the indicated task. Voordat introduces a subordinate time clause. Vertrekt retains -t because je precedes the verb inside that clause.

We hadden het boekjaar al afgesloten..scenario: You are recalling a past financial review. Explain that your group had already closed the financial year before that review began.

answers.text: We hadden het boekjaar al afgesloten.
answers.english: We'd already closed the financial year.
answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. The other verb normally occurs toward the end. We is first and hadden second; the object and al stand before afgesloten. Afsluiten is separable: sluiten af; its participle is afgesloten, with ge- inserted after af. Boekjaar is a het-word inherited from jaar. Past perfect hadden afgesloten puts closing the accounts before another past event.

answers.text: Wij hadden het boekjaar al afgesloten.
answers.english: We'd already closed the financial year.
answers.explanation: Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Ik denk na over het doel..scenario: Someone asks what you are considering. Explain that you are thinking carefully about the goal.

answers.text: Ik denk na over het doel.
answers.english: I'm thinking carefully about the goal.
answers.explanation: Ik comes first and denk second. The separated particle na appears before the over-phrase describing the topic. Nadenken is separable: ik denk na. Nadenken over means reflect on. Doel is a het-word. The present expresses current reflection; na belongs to the verb and is not the time preposition after here.

Ik blijf hier staan..scenario: Someone asks whether you will change position. Say that you will remain standing here.

answers.explanation: Ik is first and blijf second; hier locates the continuing posture, and staan is the final infinitive. Blijven + infinitive expresses continuing an activity or posture without te. Staan means stand; hier is a place adverb. Blijf has no -t with ik.

Ze praten over de kwaliteit, niet over d.scenario: A group is discussing the quality of an item, rather than its colour. Tell someone which subject they are discussing and which they are not.

answers.text: Ze praten over de kwaliteit, niet over de kleur.
answers.english: They're talking about the quality, not the colour.
answers.explanation: Ze is first and praten second. A second over-phrase contrasts the excluded topic after niet. Plural praten makes ze mean they. Over introduces a conversation topic. Niet can negate a whole prepositional phrase for an explicit contrast. Kwaliteit and kleur are de-words.

answers.text: Zij praten over de kwaliteit, niet over de kleur.
answers.english: They're talking about the quality, not the colour.
answers.explanation: Zij and ze refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Laat me even kijken..scenario: Someone has an item you want to inspect briefly. Ask them to let you have a quick look.

answers.english: Let me have a quick look.
answers.explanation: An instruction starts with the verb. Laat begins the request; me is the person who will look, even softens the request, and kijken is final. Laten takes an infinitive without te. Me is an object form in the main clause and the understood subject of kijken. Even here means for a brief moment and softens the request, not the English adjective even.

Ons bedrijf waardeert diversiteit..scenario: You are discussing your company's values. Explain that your company values diversity.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Ons bedrijf is first and waardeert is second; diversiteit is the object. Bedrijf is a singular het-word, so our is ons. The singular company requires waardeert with -t. Diversiteit is an abstract noun used without an article here. Waarderen means value/appreciate.

Dat is zijn computer..scenario: Someone asks whose computer that is. Point to it and explain that it belongs to a man already mentioned.

answers.explanation: Dat is the subject, is is second, and zijn computer identifies the object being pointed out. Dat stands independently; it does not have to agree with de computer. Zijn is possessive before computer, not the verb zijn. A possessive replaces the article.

Kun je even praten?.scenario: You want a brief conversation with a colleague. Ask informally whether they can talk for a moment.

answers.english: Can you talk for a moment?
answers.explanation: Kun starts the yes/no question, subject je follows it, and praten is the final infinitive. Kun je is an informal inverted form. Even softens the request and suggests a brief conversation. Praten after kunnen is an infinitive without te. This context asks about availability rather than physical speech ability.

answers.english: Can you talk for a moment?
answers.explanation: Jij and je refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

answers.english: Can you talk for a moment?
answers.explanation: Kun je and kan je are both standard forms of kunnen with subject je. The action still follows as an infinitive.

answers.english: Could you talk for a moment?
answers.explanation: Zou je ... kunnen + infinitive phrases the same request more tentatively/politely. Kunnen is an infinitive after zou; the action also remains an infinitive. This is a present polite request, not a report about a past ability.

Ze is blij met haar nieuwe baan..scenario: A woman has a new job and is pleased with it. Tell someone how she feels about her new job.

answers.text: Ze is blij met haar nieuwe baan.
answers.english: She's happy with her new job.
answers.explanation: Ze comes first and is second; blij is followed by met and the thing she is happy with. Blij zijn met is the normal combination for satisfaction with something. Haar is possessive. Baan is a de-word, so the adjective is nieuwe. The singular is makes ze mean she.

answers.text: Zij is blij met haar nieuwe baan.
answers.english: She's happy with her new job.
answers.explanation: Zij and ze refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Hij stuurde mij een e-mail..scenario: You received an email from a man earlier. Tell someone that he sent you an email.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Hij is first and stuurde second. Recipient mij comes before the full object een e-mail. Stuurde is singular simple past of sturen. Mij is a stressed recipient object form; me is also possible. The indirect object does not require aan when placed before the direct object here.

answers.text: Hij heeft mij een e-mail gestuurd.
answers.explanation: Heeft ... gestuurd is perfect. Mij is the recipient object; een e-mail is the thing sent.
Me is the unstressed object form corresponding to full mij. The receiver or other object remains the same; the original full form can carry emphasis.

Ze hebben je een brief geschreven..scenario: Some people have written a letter to the person you are addressing. Tell that person what they have written to them.

answers.text: Ze hebben je een brief geschreven.
answers.english: They have written you a letter.
answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. The other verb normally occurs toward the end. Ze is first and hebben second. Recipient je and the letter stand before final geschreven. Hebben geschreven is a perfect. Schrijven has irregular participle geschreven. Je is an object recipient here, not possessive, because it is not a determiner of een brief. Plural hebben makes ze mean they.

answers.text: Zij hebben je een brief geschreven.
answers.english: They have written you a letter.
answers.explanation: Zij and ze refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Kleding kopen is duur..scenario: Someone is discussing the cost of shopping. Explain that buying clothes is expensive.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. The whole activity Kleding kopen is the first constituent. Is is second, followed by the predicate duur. Kleding is an uncountable collective noun in Dutch. The infinitive phrase is a singular activity subject. Duur is predicative without -e. The object kleding comes before the infinitive kopen inside the subject phrase.

Ze zullen u bellen zodra de bestelling k.scenario: A group will telephone someone as soon as an order is ready. Tell that person, using formal address, when the group will call them.

answers.text: Ze zullen u bellen zodra de bestelling klaar is.
answers.english: They'll call you as soon as the order is ready.
answers.explanation: Ze zullen starts the main clause; u is the person called and bellen closes its verb group. In the zodra-clause, the finite is follows the subject and klaar. Zullen agrees with plural ze, not object u. Zodra means as soon as and introduces a subordinate clause. Klaar is a predicate adjective with no -e. The time clause follows the main infinitive naturally.

answers.text: Zij zullen u bellen zodra de bestelling klaar is.
answers.english: They'll call you as soon as the order is ready.
answers.explanation: Zij and ze refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Wat was zijn feedback?.scenario: A man gave feedback earlier. Ask what his feedback was.

answers.explanation: Wat asks for the content; was is second and zijn feedback follows as the subject phrase. Was is singular past of zijn. Zijn is possessive before feedback. Feedback is normally uncountable in this use; the possessive supplies the determiner.

Deel alstublieft uw scherm..scenario: You are speaking formally during an online meeting. Politely tell another participant to share their screen.

answers.explanation: Deel starts the imperative, alstublieft makes the request polite, and uw scherm is the object. The ordinary imperative is the stem deel. Uw is the polite possessive before scherm; u is a personal pronoun. Het scherm is a het-word, but a possessive replaces the article. Scherm delen has the digital sharing meaning here.

Zij heeft ons de borg teruggegeven..scenario: A woman returned a refundable deposit to your group. Tell someone what she returned to you.

answers.text: Zij heeft ons de borg teruggegeven.
answers.english: She returned the deposit to us.
answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. The other verb normally occurs toward the end. Zij is first and heeft second. The short recipient ons precedes the full object de borg, followed by teruggegeven. Teruggeven uses hebben in the perfect and separable participle teruggegeven. Borg here means a refundable deposit, not a person guaranteeing a debt. The singular auxiliary heeft agrees with zij meaning she.

answers.text: Zij gaf ons de borg terug.
answers.english: She returned the deposit to us.
answers.explanation: Teruggeven separates as gaf ... terug in simple past. Borg is a refundable deposit in this situation.

answers.text: Ze heeft ons de borg teruggegeven.
answers.english: She returned the deposit to us.
answers.explanation: Ze and zij refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Dit is mijn verantwoordelijkheid..scenario: Someone asks who is responsible for a particular duty. Identify it as your responsibility.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Dit is first and is second; mijn verantwoordelijkheid identifies the duty being pointed to. Verantwoordelijkheid is a de-word, but independent dit does not need to agree with it. Mijn is possessive. The noun refers to responsibility for a duty, rather than blame for a specific mistake in this scenario.

Ik zal het rapport versturen..scenario: A report needs to be sent. Tell your colleague that you will send the report.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. The other verb normally occurs toward the end. Ik is first and zal second; the object stands before final versturen. Versturen is inseparable because of ver-; the infinitive remains whole. Rapport is a het-word. Zal expresses the speaker’s future commitment; its plural counterpart is zullen.

Hoe betrouwbaar is deze meting?.scenario: You are discussing a particular measurement. Ask how reliable this measurement is.

answers.explanation: Hoe betrouwbaar is one question constituent, so is is second even though two words precede it. Deze meting is the subject. Betrouwbaar is predicative without -e. Meting is a de-word, so use deze. Hoe asks about the degree of reliability. A measurement’s reliability differs from whether a person is honest.

Positief blijven is belangrijk..scenario: A colleague is discouraged. Explain that remaining positive is important.

answers.explanation: Positief blijven is the first constituent and activity subject; is is second and belangrijk describes that activity. Blijven with an adjective means remain in a state. Positief remains uninflected as a predicative complement inside the subject phrase. The activity subject takes singular is.

Ben je bezig met de voorbereiding?.scenario: You see a colleague preparing for something. Ask informally whether they are busy with the preparation.

answers.text: Ben je bezig met de voorbereiding?
answers.english: Are you busy with the preparation?
answers.explanation: Ben starts the yes/no question, followed by subject je, bezig, and the activity with met. Ben je is the inverted informal form of zijn. Bezig zijn met names an activity in progress. Voorbereiding is a de-word. Bezig is predicative and takes no -e.

answers.text: Ben jij bezig met de voorbereiding?
answers.english: Are you busy with the preparation?
answers.explanation: Jij and je refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Hij legde zijn theorie uit..scenario: You are recalling a man's explanation. Explain that he explained his theory.

answers.explanation: Hij is first and legde second. The object stands between legde and the final separable particle uit. Uitleggen is separable: legt uit; its singular past is legde uit. The doubled g in leggen reduces to one g before -de. Zijn is possessive before theorie.

Controleer alstublieft mijn werk..scenario: You have completed some work and want it checked. Politely tell the person, using formal politeness, to check your work.

answers.explanation: An instruction starts with the verb. Controleer begins the instruction/request, followed by alstublieft and the object mijn werk. Controleren has stem controleer. Alstublieft adds polite tone; it does not require a subject pronoun in an ordinary imperative. Mijn replaces the article before werk.

Praat nu, want straks begint de vergader.scenario: There is time to speak now, but the meeting starts shortly. Tell someone to talk now and give that reason.

answers.text: Praat nu, want straks begint de vergadering.
answers.english: Talk now, because the meeting starts shortly.
answers.explanation: Praat nu is an imperative clause. After coordinating want, the second clause keeps main-clause order: straks first, begint second, then de vergadering. Want gives a reason without introducing subordinate verb-final order. Beginnen has singular begint. Straks means shortly/later soon, in contrast with nu.

Wat is zijn volgende zet?.scenario: A man is deciding what strategic action to take. Ask what his next move is.

answers.explanation: Wat asks which action is next; is is second and zijn volgende zet follows as the subject. Zet means a strategic move in this context, not a seat or the verb put. De zet takes attributive volgende after possessive zijn. Zijn is possessive.

Hoe laat komt hij aan?.scenario: A man is due to arrive. Ask what time he arrives.

answers.explanation: Hoe laat is one question phrase; komt is second, followed by hij and final aan. Aankomen is separable: komt aan. The present can refer to a planned arrival. Komt retains -t with subject hij after it; the informal jij inversion exception does not apply to hij.

We moeten competitief blijven..scenario: Your group faces competition and cannot afford to lose its competitive position. Explain that you have to remain competitive.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. The other verb normally occurs toward the end. We is first and moeten second; competitief describes the state to maintain, and blijven is final. Moeten expresses necessity, not a suggestion with should. Blijven plus an adjective means remain in a state. Competitief is predicative and does not receive -e. After moeten use blijven without te.
Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Ik stuur een uitnodiging aan alle buren..scenario: You are organising something for the neighbourhood. Say that you will send an invitation to all the neighbours.

answers.text: Ik stuur een uitnodiging aan alle buren.
answers.english: I'll send an invitation to all the neighbours.
answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Ik is first and stuur second; the object precedes the recipient aan alle buren. The present stuur can express an immediate intention. Alle is a plural determiner before buren and does not combine with een. Aan marks the recipients. Uitnodiging is an indefinite singular de-word.

Ze oefenen geduld..scenario: Several people are waiting patiently through a delay. Describe them as exercising patience.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Ze is first and oefenen second; geduld completes the fixed expression. Geduld oefenen is an established expression meaning to be patient, often while waiting. Geduld is uncountable and has no article here. Plural oefenen makes ze mean they. It need not mean a deliberate training exercise.
Zij and ze refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Hij zal hem de omleiding uitleggen..scenario: One man will explain a diversion route to another man. Tell someone who will explain it and to whom.

answers.text: Hij zal hem de omleiding uitleggen.
answers.english: He'll explain the diversion to him.
answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. The other verb normally occurs toward the end. Hij is first and zal second; short recipient hem comes before the full object, followed by uitleggen. Uitleggen is separable in a finite simple clause but stays whole as an infinitive after zal. Hem names the listener and is an object form. Omleiding means the rerouted road route in this context.

Wacht op hem bij de ingang..scenario: A man is expected at an entrance. Tell another person directly to wait for him by the entrance.

answers.text: Wacht op hem bij de ingang.
answers.english: Wait for him by the entrance.
answers.explanation: An instruction starts with the verb. Wacht starts the instruction; op hem names the person expected, and bij de ingang locates the waiting. Wachten op is a fixed combination. Hem is an object pronoun after op. Bij marks a nearby location. Ingang is a de-word. This imperative uses the stem wacht.

Ik beloof je dat ik op tijd zal zijn..scenario: Someone is concerned you will be late. Promise them that you will be on time.

answers.text: Ik beloof je dat ik op tijd zal zijn.
answers.english: I promise you that I'll be on time.
answers.explanation: Ik is first and beloof second; recipient je precedes the content clause. Its final verb group is zal zijn. Beloven can take a recipient and a dat-clause naming the promise. Je is an object pronoun. Op tijd means on time. In the subordinate future group, zal zijn is standard; zijn zal is also possible.

Ik zie je morgen bij de halte..scenario: You and a friend have arranged to meet tomorrow by the stop. Tell that friend when and where you will see them.

answers.text: Ik zie je morgen bij de halte.
answers.english: I'll see you tomorrow at the stop.
answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Ik is first and zie second; je is followed by the planned time and meeting place. Zien has the irregular ik form zie. Je is an object pronoun here. The future time morgen makes the present express a planned meeting. Halte is a de-word; bij means by/near.

answers.text: Morgen zie ik je bij de halte.
answers.english: I'll see you tomorrow at the stop.
answers.explanation: The time phrase and subject exchange main-clause positions around the finite verb. One whole constituent is first, the finite verb is second, and the subject follows it if time is first. The event and time are unchanged.

Draag alstublieft de mappen voor mij..scenario: You are carrying too much. Politely tell someone to carry the folders for you.

answers.text: Draag alstublieft de mappen voor mij.
answers.english: Please carry the folders for me.
answers.explanation: Draag starts the imperative; alstublieft softens it. The object precedes the beneficiary voor mij. Dragen has stem draag and irregular participle gedragen. Mappen is the plural of de map, with doubled p preserving the short vowel. Mij is the stressed object pronoun after voor.

answers.text: Draag alstublieft de mappen voor me.
answers.english: Please carry the folders for me.
answers.explanation: Me is the unstressed object form corresponding to full mij. The receiver or other object remains the same; the original full form can carry emphasis.

Ik ben hier om aan het renovatieproject.scenario: Someone asks why you have come to the site. Explain that you are here to work on the renovation project.

answers.text: Ik ben hier om aan het renovatieproject te werken.
answers.english: I'm here to work on the renovation project.
answers.explanation: Ik is first and ben second; the purpose phrase follows hier and ends with te werken. Om ... te gives the purpose. Werken aan introduces the project being worked on. Renovatieproject is one compound and takes het from project. The project phrase precedes te werken.

Start dit programma na de installatie..scenario: Someone is installing a program. Tell them to start this program after the installation.

answers.text: Start dit programma na de installatie.
answers.explanation: Start begins the instruction, followed by its object and a time prepositional phrase. Programma is a het-word, so attributive this is dit. Start is the imperative stem. Na here means after, not the separable particle of nadenken. Installatie is a de-word.

Ze richten zich op hun werk..scenario: A group is concentrating on its work. Explain what they are focusing on.

answers.text: Ze richten zich op hun werk.
answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Ze is first and richten second; reflexive zich comes before op hun werk. Zich richten op means focus on. The reflexive matches plural ze; with ik it is me. Hun is possessive before werk. Op belongs to the fixed expression.

answers.text: Zij richten zich op hun werk.
answers.explanation: Zij and ze refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Hij vertrok vroeg omdat de trein uitviel.scenario: You are recounting why a man departed early. Explain that he left early because the train was cancelled.

answers.text: Hij vertrok vroeg omdat de trein uitviel.
answers.english: He left early because the train was cancelled.
answers.explanation: Hij is first and vertrok second. In the omdat-clause, subject de trein precedes final uitviel. Vertrok is irregular singular past of vertrekken. Omdat introduces a subordinate reason clause. Uitvallen is separable, but in this verb-final subordinate clause its finite past uitviel stays together. A train uitvallen means not running/cancelled.

Wat is de beste aanpak?.scenario: Several approaches have been proposed. Ask which approach is best.

answers.explanation: Wat asks for the chosen method; is is second and the subject follows. Aanpak is a de-word. Beste is the irregular superlative of goed and takes the attributive -e ending. De beste aanpak identifies the most suitable method among alternatives.

Ik ga de kapotte rits repareren..scenario: A zip is broken and you intend to repair it. Tell someone what you are going to repair.

answers.text: Ik ga de kapotte rits repareren.
answers.english: I'm going to repair the broken zip.
answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. The other verb normally occurs toward the end. Ik is first and ga second; the object stands before final repareren. Gaan + infinitive here states an intention, without requiring physical travel. Repareren takes no te after ga. Rits is a de-word, so the attributive adjective is kapotte.

Laten we onze voortgang bekijken..scenario: Your group needs to assess how far it has got. Suggest reviewing your progress together.

answers.explanation: A suggestion with Laten we starts with the verb laten; the other verb (the infinitive) normally occurs toward the end. Laten we introduces a shared suggestion; the object comes before final bekijken. Voortgang is a de-word, so our is onze. Bekijken is inseparable because of be- and stays whole. It means examine/review here, rather than simply look casually.
Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.
Zullen we + infinitive offers the shared activity as a question. Laten we introduces it as a let’s-suggestion. Both fit proposing this joint activity; neither reports a completed event.

Is dit jouw beslissing?.scenario: A colleague has announced a decision. Ask whether this is their own decision, using informal address.

answers.explanation: Is begins the yes/no question; independent dit is the subject and jouw beslissing identifies the choice. Jouw is a stressed possessive, appropriate when contrasting whose decision it is. Jou would be an object pronoun. Beslissing is a de-word, but independent dit need not agree with it.
Jouw and possessive je both mean your here. Jouw is the full form and can emphasise ownership; je is unstressed. This je is not the subject.

Hij is bezig met het controleren van de.scenario: A man is occupied with checking the time right now. Describe what he is doing.

answers.text: Hij is bezig met het controleren van de tijd.
answers.explanation: Hij is first and is second; bezig met is followed by a nominalised activity phrase. Het controleren is an infinitive used as a noun. Van de tijd names what is checked in the nominal construction; ordinary verb form would be de tijd controleren. Bezig met presents current involvement.

answers.text: Hij is bezig de tijd te controleren.
answers.english: He is busy checking the time.
answers.explanation: The te-infinitive version uses de tijd as the object. Both explain what is occupying him now.

Ik vond je idee leuk..scenario: A colleague suggested an idea earlier and you liked it. Tell that colleague how you felt about their idea.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Ik is first and vond second; je idee is the object and leuk evaluates it. Vinden in this construction means consider/find something nice. Vond is irregular singular past. Je is possessive. Leuk is an object predicate with no -e; it does not stand attributively before idee.

Bevestig alstublieft uw boeking..scenario: You are speaking formally to a guest about their reservation. Politely tell them to confirm their booking.

answers.explanation: An instruction starts with the verb. Bevestig begins the request, followed by alstublieft and uw boeking. Bevestigen has stem bevestig. Uw is polite possessive. Boeking is a de-word meaning a reservation; it is not the noun boek meaning book. The prefix be- is inseparable.

We denken na over het risico van deze in.scenario: Your group has not made an investment decision yet. Explain that you are considering the risk of this investment.

answers.text: We denken na over het risico van deze investering.
answers.english: We're considering the risk of this investment.
answers.explanation: We is first and denken second; na is separated from the verb, followed by the full topic phrase. Nadenken over means reflect on. Risico is a het-word; investering is a de-word and takes deze. Van specifies which risk is considered.

answers.text: Wij denken na over het risico van deze investering.
answers.english: We're considering the risk of this investment.
answers.explanation: Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Wat is ons concurrentievoordeel ten opzi.scenario: You work for a small company. Ask what advantage your company has compared with larger companies.

answers.text: Wat is ons concurrentievoordeel ten opzichte van grotere bedrijven?
answers.english: What's our competitive advantage compared with larger companies?
answers.explanation: Wat is first and is second; the subject is followed by a comparison phrase naming the competitors. Concurrentievoordeel is one compound with het voordeel as its head, so possessive our is ons. Ten opzichte van means relative to/compared with. Grotere is an attributive comparative before plural bedrijven.

Zal deze oplossing werken?.scenario: Someone has proposed a solution, but it has not been tested. Ask whether this solution will work.

answers.explanation: Zal starts the yes/no question, followed by its subject and final infinitive werken. Werken here means function or succeed, not perform a job. Oplossing is a de-word and takes deze. The singular subject requires zal. Zullen asks about a predicted result.

We hebben onze manager nodig om dit conf.scenario: Your group cannot resolve a conflict alone. Explain that you need your manager to resolve this conflict.

answers.text: We hebben onze manager nodig om dit conflict op te lossen.
answers.english: We need our manager to resolve this conflict.
answers.explanation: We is first and hebben second. The need expression ends with nodig, followed by the purpose clause. Manager is a de-word, so possessive our is onze. Conflict is a het-word and takes dit. Oplossen is separable; te goes between op and lossen in the purpose infinitive.

answers.text: Wij hebben onze manager nodig om dit conflict op te lossen.
answers.english: We need our manager to resolve this conflict.
answers.explanation: Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Laten we ons succes vieren..scenario: Your group has achieved a shared goal. Suggest celebrating your group's success.

answers.explanation: A suggestion with Laten we starts with the verb laten; the other verb (the infinitive) normally occurs toward the end. Laten we introduces the shared proposal; ons succes precedes final vieren. Succes is a singular het-word, so our is ons. Vieren is an infinitive after Laten we. The proposal includes the speaker and colleagues in celebrating a completed success.
Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.
Zullen we + infinitive offers the shared activity as a question. Laten we introduces it as a let’s-suggestion. Both fit proposing this joint activity; neither reports a completed event.

Dit is erg belangrijk voor onze samenwer.scenario: Something being discussed matters greatly to how your group works together. Explain its importance for your cooperation.

answers.text: Dit is erg belangrijk voor onze samenwerking.
answers.english: This is very important for our cooperation.
answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Dit is first and is second. Erg modifies belangrijk; voor introduces what the importance concerns. Dit stands independently. Erg is a degree adverb, not an attributive adjective here. Samenwerking is a de-word and takes onze. Belangrijk is predicative without -e.

answers.text: Dit is heel belangrijk voor onze samenwerking.
answers.english: This is very important for our cooperation.
answers.explanation: Heel and erg both mean very as degree adverbs before this adjective/adverb. This changes the wording, not the stated degree or who the sentence describes.

Leg ons het verschil tussen deze materia.scenario: Your group needs to understand how some materials differ. Tell a specialist to explain the difference between these materials to your group.

answers.text: Leg ons het verschil tussen deze materialen uit.
answers.english: Explain the difference between these materials to us.
answers.explanation: An instruction starts with the verb. Leg starts the instruction and uit ends it; recipient ons and the full object stand inside that bracket. Uitleggen is separable, with imperative leg ... uit. Verschil is a het-word; tussen names the compared items. Deze agrees with plural materialen. A short recipient naturally precedes a full noun object.

answers.text: Leg het verschil tussen deze materialen aan ons uit.
answers.english: Explain the difference between these materials to us.
answers.explanation: The recipient is expressed as aan ons after the object. Leg ... uit is still the separable imperative of uitleggen.

Heb je mijn fiets voor me gerepareerd?.scenario: A colleague was repairing your bicycle for you. Ask whether they have repaired it for you.

answers.text: Heb je mijn fiets voor me gerepareerd?
answers.english: Have you repaired my bicycle for me?
answers.explanation: Heb starts the perfect question, then je, the object and beneficiary, followed by gerepareerd. Heb je is inverted and lacks -t with subject je. Repareren uses hebben and participle gerepareerd. Mijn is possessive; me after voor is an object beneficiary pronoun.

answers.text: Heb jij mijn fiets voor me gerepareerd?
answers.english: Have you repaired my bicycle for me?
answers.explanation: Jij and je refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Zal de reparatie lang duren?.scenario: You are deciding whether to wait for a repair. Ask whether the repair will take a long time.

answers.english: Will the repair take a long time?
answers.explanation: Zal starts the question, followed by its subject, lang, and final infinitive duren. Duren concerns how long an event takes or lasts. Lang makes the intended duration question explicit; it does not assess whether a repaired object is durable. Reparatie is a singular de-word.

De klant heeft het definitieve ontwerp g.scenario: The customer has signed off the final design. Tell someone that the customer has approved the final design.

answers.text: De klant heeft het definitieve ontwerp goedgekeurd.
answers.english: The customer has approved the final design.
answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. The other verb normally occurs toward the end. De klant is first and heeft second; the object precedes final goedgekeurd. Goedkeuren is separable: keurt goed; its participle is goedgekeurd. Ontwerp is a het-word, but after definite het the adjective receives -e: definitieve. The perfect presents completed approval.

Hij maakte het werk af..scenario: You are recounting a man's completed task. Explain that he finished the work.

answers.explanation: Hij is first and maakte second; the object stands before final particle af. Afmaken is separable. Its singular past is maakte af; the participle is afgemaakt. Werk is a het-word and is the object of finishing. This simple past differs from heeft afgemaakt.
The perfect uses heeft ... afgemaakt. In the simple past, afmaken separates into maakte ... af.

Je hebt geen fout gemaakt..scenario: A colleague thinks they made a mistake, but you have checked their work. Reassure them that they have not made a mistake.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. The other verb normally occurs toward the end. Je is first and hebt second; geen fout precedes final gemaakt. Geen negates indefinite een fout: no mistake/not a mistake. Hebt gemaakt is a perfect; maken uses hebben. Je before the verb requires hebt with -t.
Jij and je refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Bel haar na de lunch..scenario: A woman needs to be contacted later. Tell another person to call her after lunch.

answers.explanation: An instruction starts with the verb. Bel begins the instruction; haar is the person called and na de lunch gives the time. Bellen directly takes a person as object. Haar is an object pronoun here, not possessive. Bel is the imperative stem, with one l; na means after.

Zijn vergadering begint spoedig..scenario: A man is due to attend a meeting shortly. Tell someone that his meeting starts soon.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Zijn vergadering is first and begint second; spoedig gives the approaching time. Zijn is possessive, not a verb. Vergadering is singular, requiring begint. Spoedig means soon and has a relatively formal tone; binnenkort or straks can fit different time frames.

The time phrase and subject exchange main-clause positions around the finite verb. One whole constituent is first, the finite verb is second, and the subject follows it if time is first. The event and time are unchanged.

Wie belt er?.scenario: You hear that someone is telephoning. Ask who is calling.

answers.explanation: Wie is the question subject, followed by belt and presentative er; no additional subject pronoun is needed. Wie normally takes singular agreement in this unspecified question. Er is common in presentative subject questions and need not be translated as a literal place. Belt can mean telephones here.

Wat zijn de belangrijkste inzichten?.scenario: Your group has completed a learning activity. Ask what the most important insights are.

answers.explanation: Wat asks for the content, zijn is second, and the plural subject follows. Inzichten is plural, so the verb is zijn. Belangrijkste is the attributive superlative of belangrijk. Inzicht means understanding or insight, not a physical view in this context.

Wat is de datum van de inschrijving?.scenario: You need to know the date for registration. Ask what the registration date is.

answers.text: Wat is de datum van de inschrijving?
answers.explanation: Wat is first and is second; the full date phrase is the subject. Datum is a de-word. Van de inschrijving specifies which date is requested, rather than asking for today’s date. Inschrijving means registration in this context.

Heb je me de factuur gestuurd?.scenario: You need an invoice from a colleague. Ask whether they have sent you the invoice.

answers.text: Heb je me de factuur gestuurd?
answers.english: Have you sent me the invoice?
answers.explanation: Heb starts the perfect question; subject je, recipient me and the full object come before gestuurd. Sturen uses hebben and participle gestuurd. Heb je loses -t with the following informal subject. Factuur is a de-word. A short indirect object naturally precedes a full direct object.

answers.text: Heb jij me de factuur gestuurd?
answers.english: Have you sent me the invoice?
answers.explanation: Jij and je refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Ik wil de beschadigde stoel repareren..scenario: A chair is damaged and you want to repair it. Explain that you want to repair the damaged chair.

answers.text: Ik wil de beschadigde stoel repareren.
answers.english: I want to repair the damaged chair.
answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. The other verb normally occurs toward the end. Ik is first and wil second; the damaged chair stands before final repareren. Willen means want, not the English future will. Repareren takes no te after wil. Beschadigde is an attributive participle/adjective before de stoel.

Zij delen hun ideeën..scenario: Several people are exchanging ideas. Explain that they share their ideas.

answers.explanation: Zij is the subject in first position and the finite verb delen is second; hun ideeën is the object and follows the verb. Plural delen makes zij mean they. Hun is possessive before ideeën. Idee has plural ideeën with a diaeresis to show the vowel begins a new syllable.
