Ze and zij refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Kunt u me erdoorheen leiden?.scenario: You do not understand a procedure already mentioned. Politely ask someone, using formal address, to guide you through it.

answers.english: Could you guide me through it?
answers.explanation: A yes/no question starts with the finite verb, so no constituent comes before it. Kunt starts the request, followed by u and me; erdoorheen specifies the process and leiden is final. Leiden means guide/lead, not lijden meaning suffer. Erdoorheen refers back to the procedure: through it. Kunt u is standard; kan u is also standard. The infinitive follows the modal without te.

answers.english: Could you guide me through it?
answers.explanation: Kunt u and kan u are both standard; kan u is particularly common in Belgium. U keeps polite address and the action remains an infinitive.

answers.text: Zou u me erdoorheen kunnen leiden?
answers.english: Could you guide me through it?
answers.explanation: Zou u ... kunnen + infinitive phrases the same request more tentatively/politely. Kunnen is an infinitive after zou; the action also remains an infinitive. This is a present polite request, not a report about a past ability.

Heeft u zijn werk beoordeeld?.scenario: A supervisor was evaluating a man's work. Politely ask whether they have assessed his work.

answers.explanation: Heeft starts the perfect question, followed by polite subject u, object and final beoordeeld. Heeft u and hebt u are both standard. Beoordelen is inseparable with participle beoordeeld, without added ge-. Zijn is possessive; werk is the object rather than the subject.
Heeft u and hebt u are both standard with polite subject u. This is not the informal heb je inversion pattern.

Bedankt voor uw geduld tijdens het wacht.scenario: Someone you address formally has waited patiently during a delay. Thank them specifically for their patience while waiting.

answers.text: Bedankt voor uw geduld tijdens het wachten.
answers.english: Thank you for your patience while waiting.
answers.explanation: Bedankt begins a conventional thanks expression without a finite verb; the following phrases name the reason and time. Bedankt voor is a standard polite expression. Uw is possessive. Geduld is uncountable; het wachten is a nominalised infinitive after tijdens. It is natural standalone thanks, not a finite full clause.

Koop de treinkaart voor hem..scenario: A man needs a train ticket, but cannot buy it himself. Tell another person to buy the ticket for him.

answers.english: Buy the train ticket for him.
answers.explanation: An instruction starts with the verb. Koop starts the instruction; the object comes before beneficiary voor hem. Kopen has stem koop. Voor names the person benefiting from the purchase. Hem is an object form after the preposition. Treinkaart is a compound with de kaart as its head.

Ze heeft mijn idee gestolen..scenario: A woman has presented your idea as her own. Tell someone that she has stolen your idea.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. The other verb normally occurs toward the end. Ze is first and heeft second; mijn idee stands before final gestolen. Stelen has irregular participle gestolen and uses hebben. Singular heeft makes ze mean she. Mijn is possessive. Een idee stelen is figurative taking credit for someone else’s idea.
Zij and ze refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Hij werkte heel hard..scenario: You are recounting a man's effort on a task. Explain that he worked very hard.

answers.explanation: Hij is first and werkte second; heel modifies manner adverb hard. Werken has singular past werkte with -te. Hard describes effort rather than the physical hardness of an object. Heel means very and modifies hard; both are adverbial here.
Heel and erg both mean very as degree adverbs before this adjective/adverb. This changes the wording, not the stated degree or who the sentence describes.

Je zag er erg vermoeid uit..scenario: You are talking to someone about how they looked earlier. Tell them that they looked very tired.

answers.text: Je zag er erg vermoeid uit.
answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Je is first and zag second; er and uit surround the appearance description. Er ... uitzien describes appearance. Zag is irregular past of zien; uit separates in a main clause. Er belongs to the appearance construction and is not a literal place. Vermoeid is predicative without -e.

answers.text: Jij zag er erg vermoeid uit.
answers.explanation: Jij and je refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

answers.text: Je zag er heel vermoeid uit.
answers.explanation: Heel and erg both mean very as degree adverbs before this adjective/adverb. This changes the wording, not the stated degree or who the sentence describes.

Breng de monsters naar het laboratorium..scenario: Some test samples need to reach a laboratory. Tell another person to take the samples to the laboratory.

answers.text: Breng de monsters naar het laboratorium.
answers.english: Take the samples to the laboratory.
answers.explanation: An instruction starts with the verb. Breng starts the instruction; the object precedes the destination naar het laboratorium. Brengen has stem breng and irregular participle gebracht. Monsters means test samples here, not mythical creatures. Laboratorium is a het-word. Naar marks the destination.

Wat is het algemene doel van deze opleid.scenario: You are starting a training course. Ask what the overall aim of this particular course is.

answers.text: Wat is het algemene doel van deze opleiding?
answers.english: What's the overall aim of this training course?
answers.explanation: Wat asks for the aim; is is second and the complete subject phrase follows. Doel is a het-word, but definite het requires attributive algemene with -e. Opleiding is a de-word and takes deze. Van specifies the course whose aim is asked about.

Hoeveel tijd hebben we?.scenario: Your group must finish an activity before another appointment. Ask how much time your group has.

answers.english: How much time do we have?
answers.explanation: Hoeveel tijd is the first question constituent and object; hebben is second and subject we follows. Tijd is uncountable in this quantity use. Hoeveel asks for an amount; many countable hours would be hoeveel uur. Plural subject we requires hebben.

answers.english: How much time do we have?
answers.explanation: Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Mag ik mijn laptop gebruiken?.scenario: You are attending a session where device use may be restricted. Ask permission to use your laptop.

answers.explanation: Mag starts the permission question; ik and the object follow, and gebruiken is final. Mogen expresses permission, whereas kunnen primarily expresses ability or possibility. Mijn is possessive. Gebruiken after mag takes no te. Mag is singular present of mogen.

Haar computer is offline..scenario: A woman's computer is not connected to the network. Explain that her computer is offline, without claiming the computer is broken.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Haar computer is the first constituent; is is second and offline describes its connection state. Haar is possessive, not an object pronoun here. Computer is singular, requiring is. Offline means not connected to the network; it does not necessarily mean the machine is broken.

Dit werkblad is gemakkelijk schoon te ma.scenario: You are discussing a particular worktop. Explain that this worktop is easy to clean.

answers.text: Dit werkblad is gemakkelijk schoon te maken.
answers.english: This worktop is easy to clean.
answers.explanation: Dit werkblad is first and is second; gemakkelijk is followed by the final infinitive phrase schoon te maken. Werkblad is a het-word, so use dit. Schoonmaken is separable, with te between schoon and maken. Gemakkelijk is predicative without -e. The worktop is what gets cleaned.

answers.text: Dit werkblad is makkelijk schoon te maken.
answers.english: This worktop is easy to clean.
answers.explanation: Gemakkelijk and makkelijk are synonymous here; makkelijk is especially common in conversation. Neither changes the action described.

Dit is onze agenda voor de studiedag..scenario: You are showing the agreed schedule for your group's training day. Identify it as your agenda for that day.

answers.text: Dit is onze agenda voor de studiedag.
answers.english: This is our agenda for the training day.
answers.explanation: Independent Dit is first and is second; the following noun phrase identifies the schedule of activities. Agenda here means the planned list of items/sessions, not a personal appointment diary. It is a de-word and takes onze. Dit stands independently and need not agree with agenda. Studiedag is a compound ending in de dag.

We werkten op kantoor..scenario: You are recalling where your group worked earlier. Explain that you worked at the office.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. We is first and werkten second; op kantoor gives the workplace. Werkten is plural simple past of werken, with -ten. Op kantoor is a conventional workplace expression without an article. It does not mean physically standing on top of an office.
Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Ik begrijp waarom je twijfelt..scenario: A colleague has explained their doubts to you. Tell them that you understand why they are unsure.

answers.english: I understand why you are unsure.
answers.explanation: Ik is first and begrijp second; the embedded why-clause is its object, with twijfelt final. Begrijpen is inseparable because of be-. Waarom introduces an embedded question, not a direct question with inversion. Je before its finite verb requires twijfelt with -t. Twijfelen means doubt or hesitate.

Dit fietspad is erg veilig..scenario: You are pointing to a cycle path protected from traffic. Describe this cycle path as very safe.

answers.english: This cycle path is very safe.
answers.explanation: Dit fietspad is one phrase in first position and the finite verb is second; erg modifies the predicate adjective veilig, which stays at the end. Fietspad is a het-word, so this is dit before the noun. Veilig is predicative without -e. Erg means very as a degree adverb.

answers.english: This cycle path is very safe.
answers.explanation: Heel and erg both mean very as degree adverbs before this adjective/adverb. This changes the wording, not the stated degree or who the sentence describes.

Is dit uw verslag van het ongeval?.scenario: You are speaking formally to someone who may have written an accident report. Ask whether this is their report of the accident.

answers.text: Is dit uw verslag van het ongeval?
answers.english: Is this your report of the accident?
answers.explanation: Is starts the question; independent dit is subject and the report phrase follows it. Uw is polite possessive; u is a personal pronoun. Verslag and ongeval are het-words. Van specifies the event described. Independent dit is not an attributive demonstrative of verslag.

Hij verkoopt zijn fiets aan hen..scenario: A man is selling his bicycle to several people. Explain what he is selling and to whom.

answers.text: Hij verkoopt zijn fiets aan hen.
answers.english: He sells his bicycle to them.
answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Hij is first and verkoopt second; the sold item precedes recipient aan hen. Verkopen is inseparable and takes third-person verkoopt. Hen is the standard stressed plural object form after a preposition; unstressed ze is also possible. Zijn is possessive before fiets.

Wat is je plan voor de verhuizing?.scenario: A friend will move home, but has not explained their arrangements. Ask what their plan is for the move.

answers.text: Wat is je plan voor de verhuizing?
answers.english: What's your plan for the move?
answers.explanation: Wat is the question word in first position and the finite verb is second; the phrase after it is the subject, so a question word does not change the verb-second rule. Je is possessive before plan, not the subject of is. Plan is a het-word. Voor specifies the move the plan concerns. Verhuizing is a de-word.

Kunt u mij het rapport sturen?.scenario: You need a report that someone else has. Politely ask them, using formal address, to send you the report.

answers.text: Kunt u mij het rapport sturen?
answers.english: Could you send me the report?
answers.explanation: A yes/no question starts with the finite verb, so no constituent comes before it. Kunt starts the request; u, recipient mij and the object come before final sturen. Kunt u and kan u are both standard. Mij is a stressed recipient object, with me possible unstressed. Sturen after a modal is an infinitive without te. Rapport is a het-word.

answers.text: Kan u mij het rapport sturen?
answers.english: Could you send me the report?
answers.explanation: Kunt u and kan u are both standard; kan u is particularly common in Belgium. U keeps polite address and the action remains an infinitive.

answers.text: Zou u mij het rapport kunnen sturen?
answers.english: Could you send me the report?
answers.explanation: Zou u ... kunnen + infinitive phrases the same request more tentatively/politely. Kunnen is an infinitive after zou; the action also remains an infinitive. This is a present polite request, not a report about a past ability.

answers.text: Kunt u me het rapport sturen?
answers.english: Could you send me the report?
answers.explanation: Me is the unstressed object form corresponding to full mij. The receiver or other object remains the same; the original full form can carry emphasis.

Wat is hun grootste obstakel bij het vin.scenario: A group is struggling to find accommodation. Ask what their greatest obstacle is in finding housing.

answers.text: Wat is hun grootste obstakel bij het vinden van huisvesting?
answers.english: What's their biggest obstacle to finding accommodation?
answers.explanation: Wat is first and is second; the whole obstacle phrase is subject. Hun is possessive. Grootste is an attributive superlative. Het vinden is a nominalised infinitive after bij; van huisvesting names what is being found. Huisvesting is uncountable accommodation.

Mag ik je pen lenen om dit formulier te.scenario: You need to sign this form, but have no pen. Ask a person informally whether you may borrow their pen for that purpose.

answers.text: Mag ik je pen lenen om dit formulier te ondertekenen?
answers.english: May I borrow your pen to sign this form?
answers.explanation: Mag starts the permission question, then ik, je pen and lenen. The following purpose phrase ends with te ondertekenen. Mogen expresses permission. Je is possessive before pen. Lenen means borrow from the owner in this context. Ondertekenen is inseparable, so te goes before the whole infinitive. Formulier is a het-word and takes dit.

Ik ben te laat voor de laatste tram..scenario: You arrived after the final tram had departed. Explain that you are too late for the last tram.

answers.text: Ik ben te laat voor de laatste tram.
answers.english: I'm too late for the last tram.
answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Ik is first and ben second; te laat is followed by the missed event with voor. Te before laat is a degree word, not an infinitive marker. Tram is a de-word; laatste is attributive with -e. Ben is the ik form of zijn.

We moeten innovatie stimuleren..scenario: Your group wants new ideas to develop. Explain that you have to encourage innovation.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. The other verb normally occurs toward the end. We is first and moeten second; innovatie precedes final stimuleren. Moeten expresses necessity. Innovatie is an abstract uncountable noun without an article here. Stimuleren is an infinitive without te after moeten.
Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Wat is hun geheime wapen bij het bakken.scenario: Some bakers produce particularly good bread. Ask what their special strength or technique is when baking bread, using the secret-weapon metaphor.

answers.text: Wat is hun geheime wapen bij het bakken van brood?
answers.english: What's their secret weapon for baking bread?
answers.explanation: Wat is first and is second; the full figurative weapon phrase is subject. Geheime wapen is figurative for a special strength or technique. Hun is possessive. Het bakken is a nominalised infinitive after bij; van brood names what is baked. No physical weapon is meant.

Het spijt me, de koffieautomaat is kapot.scenario: A visitor wants coffee, but the machine is broken. Apologise and explain that the coffee machine is broken.

answers.text: Het spijt me, de koffieautomaat is kapot.
answers.english: I'm sorry, the coffee machine is broken.
answers.explanation: Two short main clauses are linked by a comma in this spoken-style apology. Each has its own subject and finite verb. Het spijt me is an idiomatic apology; me is the experiencer object. Koffieautomaat is a de-word. Kapot is predicative without -e. The machine being broken does not itself say who caused the damage.

Wat is het volgende getal in deze reeks?.scenario: You are looking at a sequence of numbers. Ask what the next number is in this particular sequence.

answers.text: Wat is het volgende getal in deze reeks?
answers.english: What's the next number in this sequence?
answers.explanation: Wat is first and is second; the next-number phrase follows as subject. Getal is a het-word; definite het takes attributive volgende. Reeks is a de-word and takes deze. The noun makes the omitted next thing explicit in a number-pattern situation.

Ik regel de logistiek..scenario: Your group needs someone to organise transport and practical arrangements. Offer to handle the logistics.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Ik is first and regel second; de logistiek is the direct object. Regelen has the ik form regel. Logistiek names practical organisation of movement and supplies and takes de. The present expresses a commitment in context, not necessarily an action already complete.

Wat is de volgende stap bij het aanvrage.scenario: You are applying for a permit and have completed one step. Ask what the next step is in the application process.

answers.text: Wat is de volgende stap bij het aanvragen van een vergunning?
answers.english: What's the next step in applying for a permit?
answers.explanation: Wat is first and is second; the full next-step phrase is subject. Stap is a de-word. Het aanvragen is a nominalised infinitive after bij; van een vergunning specifies what is requested. Aanvragen is separable in a finite clause, but stays whole in this activity noun.

We kijken uit naar de start van de taalc.scenario: A language course has not started yet. Explain that your group is eagerly anticipating the start of that course.

answers.text: We kijken uit naar de start van de taalcursus.
answers.english: We're looking forward to the start of the language course.
answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. We is first and kijken second; uit is separated and the anticipated event follows naar. Uitkijken naar means look forward to. This noun reference uses naar de start, unlike pronominal ernaar uitkijken. Taalcursus is a de-compound; van specifies what starts. The event is still in the future.

answers.text: Wij kijken uit naar de start van de taalcursus.
answers.english: We're looking forward to the start of the language course.
answers.explanation: Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Ik ben hier om de lift te repareren..scenario: You have arrived to fix a building's lift. Explain to someone that you are here to repair the lift.

answers.text: Ik ben hier om de lift te repareren.
answers.english: I'm here to repair the lift.
answers.explanation: Ik is first and ben second; the purpose phrase follows hier and ends with te repareren. Om ... te expresses purpose. Lift is a de-word; it is the object within the infinitive phrase. Repareren is not separable, so te stands before the whole verb.

Dit formulier is snel in te vullen..scenario: This form requires very little time to complete. Tell someone that it can be filled in quickly.

answers.text: Dit formulier is snel in te vullen.
answers.english: This form can be filled in quickly.
answers.explanation: Dit formulier is first and is second. Snel describes completing speed; in te vullen is the final infinitive phrase. Formulier is a het-word and takes dit. Invullen is separable, with te between in and vullen. The construction presents the form as something that can be completed quickly; snel is adverbial here.

Ze zullen te laat zijn voor de inschrijv.scenario: Two people are expected to miss registration. Predict that they will be too late for registration.

answers.text: Ze zullen te laat zijn voor de inschrijving.
answers.english: They'll be too late for registration.
answers.explanation: Ze is first and zullen second; te laat precedes infinitive zijn, followed by the registration phrase. Zullen agrees with plural ze. Zijn after the auxiliary is an infinitive. Te is a degree word before laat, not an infinitive marker. The sentence predicts future lateness.

answers.text: Zij zullen te laat zijn voor de inschrijving.
answers.english: They'll be too late for registration.
answers.explanation: Zij and ze refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Ik was niet op kantoor toen de levering.scenario: Someone asks why you did not receive a delivery yourself. Explain that you were not at the office when it arrived.

answers.text: Ik was niet op kantoor toen de levering aankwam.
answers.english: I wasn't at the office when the delivery arrived.
answers.explanation: Ik is first and was second. The toen-clause follows the location and ends with its finite verb aankwam. Toen refers to a particular past moment. Aankomen is separable, but finite aankwam stays whole in this subordinate clause. Op kantoor is a conventional article-free location expression.

Het is beter om op de bevestiging te wac.scenario: Your group is choosing between acting now and waiting for confirmation. Explain that waiting for confirmation is better.

answers.text: Het is beter om op de bevestiging te wachten.
answers.english: It's better to wait for confirmation.
answers.explanation: Het is first and is second; beter evaluates the action named by the following infinitive phrase. Beter is comparative better, not superlative best. Het anticipates the action clause. Wachten op is fixed; om ... te names the evaluated action here rather than the purpose of a visit. Bevestiging is a de-word.

Leg me alsjeblieft de inhoud van deze br.scenario: You cannot understand a letter. Politely ask someone informally to explain the content of this letter to you.

answers.text: Leg me alsjeblieft de inhoud van deze brief uit.
answers.english: Please explain the content of this letter to me.
answers.explanation: An instruction starts with the verb. Leg begins the instruction and uit ends it; recipient, politeness word and object stand between them. Uitleggen is separable. Inhoud is a de-word; deze agrees with de brief. Me is a recipient object. Alsjeblieft is the informal politeness word, compared with formal alstublieft.

Ik ben van plan in België te blijven won.scenario: You live in Belgium and intend to continue living there. Explain your plan to remain living in Belgium.

answers.text: Ik ben van plan in België te blijven wonen.
answers.english: I'm planning to continue living in Belgium.
answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. The other verb normally occurs toward the end. Ik is first and ben second. The intended activity follows van plan and ends with te blijven wonen. Van plan zijn takes a te-infinitive, optionally introduced by om. Blijven wonen expresses continued residence; wonen follows blijven without another te. België uses a diaeresis. This is intention, not seeking an opportunity.

Laten we over ideeën voor een buurtfeest.scenario: Your neighbours want to organise a neighbourhood party. Suggest brainstorming ideas for that party together.

answers.text: Laten we over ideeën voor een buurtfeest brainstormen.
answers.english: Let's brainstorm ideas for a neighbourhood party.
answers.explanation: A suggestion with Laten we starts with the verb laten; the other verb (the infinitive) normally occurs toward the end. Laten we introduces the shared proposal; the topic over ideas stands before final brainstormen. Brainstormen is commonly used with over for the topic. Ideeën is plural with a diaeresis. Buurtfeest is a compound ending in het feest, indefinite een here. The proposal infinitive has no te.

answers.text: Laten wij over ideeën voor een buurtfeest brainstormen.
answers.english: Let's brainstorm ideas for a neighbourhood party.
answers.explanation: Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

answers.text: Zullen we over ideeën voor een buurtfeest brainstormen?
answers.english: Shall we brainstorm ideas for a neighbourhood party?
answers.explanation: Zullen we + infinitive offers the shared activity as a question. Laten we introduces it as a let’s-suggestion. Both fit proposing this joint activity; neither reports a completed event.

Het is belangrijk om kalm te blijven tij.scenario: A disagreement is becoming heated. Explain that it is important to remain calm during a conflict.

answers.text: Het is belangrijk om kalm te blijven tijdens een conflict.
answers.english: It's important to stay calm during a conflict.
answers.explanation: Het is first and is second; belangrijk evaluates the following action/state infinitive phrase. Het anticipates the clause describing what is important. Kalm is predicative after blijven and has no -e. Om ... te names the evaluated action; tijdens introduces the time circumstance.

Deze parkeerautomaat is gemakkelijk te g.scenario: You are showing someone a particular parking meter. Explain that this parking meter is easy to use.

answers.text: Deze parkeerautomaat is gemakkelijk te gebruiken.
answers.english: This parking meter is easy to use.
answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. The other verb normally occurs toward the end. Deze parkeerautomaat is first and is second; gemakkelijk is followed by te gebruiken. Parkeerautomaat is a de-word and takes deze. Gemakkelijk is predicative without -e. The machine is the thing used in the te-infinitive construction, not the person doing the using.

answers.text: Deze parkeerautomaat is makkelijk te gebruiken.
answers.english: This parking meter is easy to use.
answers.explanation: Gemakkelijk and makkelijk are synonymous here; makkelijk is especially common in conversation. Neither changes the action described.

We moeten onze doelen op elkaar afstemme.scenario: Your group has separate objectives that must fit together. Explain that you have to align your goals with each other.

answers.text: We moeten onze doelen op elkaar afstemmen.
answers.english: We have to align our goals with each other.
answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. The other verb normally occurs toward the end. We is first and moeten second; the object and op elkaar come before final afstemmen. Afstemmen op means to coordinate with. Elkaar is reciprocal: the goals are aligned with each other. Onze agrees with plural doelen. After moeten the separable infinitive stays whole, without te.

answers.text: Wij moeten onze doelen op elkaar afstemmen.
answers.english: We have to align our goals with each other.
answers.explanation: Wij and we refer to the same subject. The full form can emphasise who acts; the unstressed form is common in ordinary speech. Subject and verb agreement remain the same.

Hij voltooide zijn opleiding zonder fina.scenario: You are recounting a man's achievement. Explain that he completed his training without financial support.

answers.explanation: Hij is first and past-tense voltooide second; the object is followed by the without phrase. Voltooien has regular past voltooide. Zijn is possessive, not a finite verb. Financiële has -e before the de-word steun. Steun is uncountable here. Zonder introduces what was absent.

Ik ben bang voor mislukking..scenario: You are discussing what worries you about attempting something important. Admit that you are afraid of failure.

answers.explanation: In a main clause the finite verb is in second position, after one first constituent. Ik is first and ben second; bang takes its fear object with voor. Dit is mijn grootste uitdaging tijdens d.scenario: You are discussing a particular difficult task during your internship. Identify it as your greatest challenge during the internship.

answers.text: Dit is mijn grootste uitdaging tijdens de stage.

answers.text: Tijdens de stage is dit mijn grootste uitdaging.
answers.english: This is my greatest challenge during the internship.
answers.explanation: The time phrase and subject exchange main-clause positions around the finite verb. One whole constituent is first, the finite verb is second, and the subject follows it if time is first. The event and time are unchanged.

We moeten de verwarming aanzetten..scenario: Your group is in a cold room and the heating is off. Explain that you have to turn on the heating.

Ik ben hier om te blijven..scenario: People wonder whether your presence here is temporary. Reassure them that you are here to stay.

We kijken uit naar het antwoord op onze.scenario: Your group has submitted a job application and is waiting hopefully. Explain that you are looking forward to the reply to your application.

Gelieve uw status bij te werken..scenario: You are writing a formal request to someone with an outdated task status. Politely tell them to update their status.

Vraag hem de weg naar het station..scenario: A man nearby knows the area. Tell a visitor to ask him for directions to the station.

Wat zijn uw verwachtingen?.scenario: You are speaking formally to a new participant. Ask what they expect from the experience.

answers.explanation: Wat is first and zijn second; plural uw verwachtingen is the subject. Verwachtingen is plural, requiring zijn. Uw is formal possessive, not subject u. Wat asks for the content of the expectations. A singular question would be Wat is uw verwachting?

answers.text: Ze is klaar om haar voorstel toe te lichten.
answers.english: She's ready to explain her proposal.

Kom je beloften na..scenario: Someone has made commitments but has not fulfilled them. Tell them directly to keep their promises.

answers.explanation: The imperative Kom begins the instruction and na closes the separable verb around its object. Nakomen means to fulfil or honour a promise. Je hebt geen verandering aangebracht..scenario: You have compared two versions and found no alteration. Tell the person who was editing it that they have not made a change.

Wat is mijn volgende stap na dit sollici.scenario: You have just finished a job interview. Ask the interviewer what your next step is after this interview.

Ik doe mijn best..scenario: A task is difficult, but you are putting in your strongest effort. Reassure someone that you are doing your best.

Ze waren niet in de kamer tijdens het ge.scenario: You are discussing an earlier conversation. Explain that the people being discussed were not in the room during that conversation.

Ik heb een woordenboek voor je gekocht..scenario: You have bought a dictionary for the person you are addressing. Tell them what you bought for them.

We zitten boven ons budget..scenario: Your group has spent more money than the budget allowed. Explain that you are over your budget.

Ik ga in de bibliotheek werken..scenario: You are preparing to do work in a library. Explain that you are going to work in the library, without saying it is your employer.

Onze kookles begint nu..scenario: You and other learners are gathered for a cooking class that starts at this moment. Tell someone that your cooking lesson begins now.
